# Downtime workers commit directly to dev in the main checkout, breaking the pushed-tip invariant

## Problem statement

Twice during epic SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 the main checkout's `dev` carried **unpushed commits made directly in the main checkout** (not through a worktree `finish`), which made `implement.py start` refuse every new worktree with `Refusing to create a worktree from local dev: it is not a known pushed tip`. Recovery required publishing the foreign commits by hand, and the pre-push full-suite gate then `gate-refused` because the main checkout was dirty with a zero-content mode change (`100644 → 100755` on `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`).

The two observed commits were:

- `57768e2fe3` — `fix(machine-hygiene): remove shebang from config.py module (EXE001)` (no work-item id in the subject)
- `981af4d849` — `fix: Wrap implicit string concatenation in persist_audit.py (SA-0MWDKRD8G008Z164)` — landed by the herdr downtime worker for an item still `open`

## Root-cause verification (producer correction, 2026-11-18)

The producer's position — **the fix belongs in the skill layer, not the herdr dispatcher** — is correct on the substance, with one precision worth recording:

- The dispatcher is **not the committer**: `buildDowntimePaneArgs` only supplies `--cwd <main checkout root>`; it never runs `git commit`.
- The two observed commits are **ad-hoc agent commits**, not skill-helper commits. Both are authored `Sorra the Orc` and neither message is produced by any skill code path. The commit helpers that *can* commit are `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (message `audit: remediate ruff false positives (per-file-ignores)`) and `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` / `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (message `Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes`).
- So the skill layer owns **both** the direct-commit helpers and the guardrails that should have stopped the ad-hoc commit. The dispatcher's `--cwd` is a contributing factor, not the defect.

Consequence for scope: option A (SorraAgents-only) is right, and AC3's **pre-commit hook** is the piece that catches ad-hoc agent commits — hardening the skill helpers alone would not have prevented either incident.

## Users

- **Herdr downtime dispatcher / downtime worker** — spawns `pi` panes with `--cwd <main checkout root>` and dispatches the `plan`, `intake`, `audit`, `implement` and `risk-effort` skills; a dispatched session that commits in that cwd poisons the shared `dev` ref for every other session.
- **Any implement session starting a worktree** — is blocked until the foreign commits are reconciled, regardless of which project or item it belongs to.
- **Producer / operator** — must currently reconcile by hand (inspect, verify, push or reset) with no attribution of which work item owns each foreign commit.

Example user stories:

- As an implement session, when I run `implement.py start`, I want a worktree created without first having to reconcile someone else's unpushed commits, so my work is never blocked by another session's shortcut.
- As a producer, when `start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed tip, I want the refusal to name the work item(s) owning the unpushed commits, so reconciliation is one step instead of a manual log trawl.
- As the downtime worker, I want a dispatched session either to work in a worktree or to push what it commits before releasing the item, so the pushed-tip invariant is never broken by automation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The committing skills (`audit` `_commit_config_remediation`; `code-review` and `code_review` `_commit_changes`) either work in a worktree, refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout, or push what they commit before releasing the item.
- `start`'s refusal names the owning work items of the unpushed commits (subject scan) so reconciliation is one step.
- A `.githooks/pre-commit` hook refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout at commit time (zero-width window — the commit is never created), with an explicit operator override for deliberate hot-fixes, and a `git_sandbox` test proves it fires in the main checkout and does not fire in a worktree or on a feature branch.
- A `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` helper lists the `origin/dev..dev` commits with their owning work items and offers push (default) or reset, and is documented in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

One direct-on-dev commit from any session blocks worktree creation for every implement session in the repository until `dev` is reconciled; the higher the fan-out, the more often this recurs.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation.** SorraAgents implementation must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start`; `finish` fails closed on writes outside it. The chosen scope (A) keeps every change inside a SorraAgents worktree.
- **Pushed-tip invariant.** `_resolve_start_base` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) deliberately refuses to branch from a local `dev` that is not a known pushed tip; that refusal must stay (it is the invariant, not the bug).
- **Fail-open on an unreachable remote.** A failed `git fetch` still branches from local `dev` (documented offline fallback) — the guard must not make offline work impossible.
- **No new blocking of legitimate finishes.** The post-push fast-forward of the main checkout's `dev` (SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR) is a fast-forward, not a commit, so the pre-commit hook must not fire on it. `wl sync` commits on `refs/worklog/data`, not `dev`, so it is also unaffected.
- **Operator override.** A deliberate operator hot-fix on `dev` in the main checkout must remain possible via an explicit opt-in (e.g. `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1`), so the hook does not become an absolute prohibition.
- **UK English** in all written output.

## Existing state

- **The dispatcher runs panes in the main checkout.** `buildDowntimePaneArgs` forwards `--cwd <worklog root>` and `spawnAgentPane`/`spawnDowntimePane` spawn the pane there (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts`). The dispatcher's skill kinds are `plan | intake | audit | implement | risk-effort`.
- **Skills that commit in their cwd.** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈ line 14222) stages the config file and runs `git commit` **locally, no push**. `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 425) and a duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈ line 641) run `git add .` + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: …"`.
- **`start` already refuses, but opaquely.** `_resolve_start_base` (`implement.py` ≈ line 8021) detects `local_dev_not_a_pushed_tip` and `phase_start` posts a comment (≈ line 12090) naming only the two tips and a three-step manual remedy — no attribution of the foreign commits to work items.
- **The pushed-tip guarantees are documented.** `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (≈ line 2638) describes the three cooperating guarantees (pre-push deferral, post-push fast-forward, ancestry assertion) and the `_resolve_start_base` refusal.
- **A placement guard exists.** `implement.py` has implementation-placement gates (`SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2`) and a read-only pre-claim foreign-mutation check of the main checkout, but they only cover sessions that go through the implement skill.
- **A dirty-checkout check exists.** `scripts/hygiene_check.sh::check_dirty_checkout` warns on a dirty main checkout, but it does not detect **committed-but-unpushed** `dev` commits.
- **A live-repo mutation guard exists.** `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` plus `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` fail a test run that mutates a live ref — a candidate precedent for AC3's guard.
- **No pre-commit hook exists.** `.githooks/` ships `pre-push`, `pre-push.v2`, `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` and `worklog-post-pull`; `core.hooksPath` is `.githooks`, so a new executable `.githooks/pre-commit` is picked up automatically. `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires and refreshes the pre-push hook idempotently — the pre-commit hook needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

1. **Close the direct-commit path (skill side).** Harden `audit`'s and `code-review`/`code_review`'s commit helpers so they refuse (or redirect to a worktree, or push before release) when they would commit on `dev` in the main checkout.
2. **Attribute the refusal.** Parse the work-item ids out of the subjects of `origin/dev..dev` and include them in the `start` refusal message and its work-item comment, so reconciliation is one step.
3. **Add the immediate guard.** Add `.githooks/pre-commit` that refuses a commit on `dev` in the main checkout (with an operator override), wire it into `scripts/install_pi.sh`, and prove it with a `git_sandbox` test.
4. **Add the reconciliation helper.** Add `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` (list with owning items; push default, reset opt-in) and document it in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.
5. **Record the dispatcher follow-up.** A ContentCreator/herdr dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is out of scope here and recorded as a linked follow-up — its worklog is not initialised (0-byte DB), mirroring the SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC cross-repo precedent.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_resolve_start_base` (≈ 8021) and the `phase_start` refusal comment (≈ 12090): add the unpushed-commit subject scan and name the owning work items.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_commit_config_remediation` (≈ 14222): refuse/redirect/push when committing on `dev` in the main checkout.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — `_commit_changes` (≈ 425) and `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈ 641): same guard (and reconcile the duplicate directory).
- `.githooks/pre-commit` — new pre-commit hook (main-checkout + `dev` detection, operator override).
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — install/refresh the pre-commit hook idempotently, beside the existing pre-push wiring.
- `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` — new reconciliation helper (list + push/reset).
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — `check_dirty_checkout` (≈ 179): optionally extend to unpushed-`dev` detection.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — reconciliation helper documentation (≈ 2638 section).
- `tests/` (e.g. `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py`) — `git_sandbox` proofs for the hook and the `start` attribution.
- `packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.ts`, `…/downtime-worker.dispatch-claims.ts`, `…/index.ts` (ContentCreator) — **out of scope**, linked follow-up only.

## Related work

- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** — finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed). Same pushed-tip invariant family.
- **SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN** — Push to dev from the worktree that holds the commit (completed). Establishes that `finish` pushes from the checkout holding the commit.
- **SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2** — Enforce git worktree usage for all implementation work (completed). Establishes the worktree requirement and the placement gate that this item extends to non-implement sessions.
- **SA-0MWFKDH78002T2CR** — deferred post-push fast-forward (referenced by the pushed-tip docs).
- **SA-0MWL51XNM001HMVC** — cross-repo hand-off precedent (herdr emitter filed in SorraAgents).
- Parent epic: **SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1** (discovered from).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Ad-hoc-commit risk (medium).** The observed incidents were ad-hoc agent commits, not skill-helper commits, so the skill-helper hardening alone is insufficient — AC3's pre-commit hook is the necessary backstop. Both must land.
- **Guard false-positive risk (medium).** The pre-commit hook must not fire on the post-push fast-forward (not a commit), on `wl sync` (commits on `refs/worklog/data`), or in a worktree/feature branch. A `git_sandbox` test must pin each case.
- **Duplicate-directory risk (medium).** `skill/code-review/` and `skill/code_review/` both exist and both commit; only `code-review` has a `SKILL.md`. Fixing one and not the other would leave a live direct-commit path.
- **Operator hot-fix risk (medium).** An absolute prohibition on committing on `dev` in the main checkout would block legitimate operator hot-fixes; the explicit override keeps that path open.
- **Scope-creep risk (medium).** The dispatcher change (spawn in a worktree) is a ContentCreator concern; record it as a linked follow-up, not scope.
- **Assumption:** the "bounded window" for AC3 is **zero-width** — the pre-commit hook refuses the commit before it exists.
- **Assumption:** the reconciliation helper's default action is `push`; `reset --hard` requires explicit confirmation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q1 — Where does the fix live (scope split)?**
- Asked: The downtime dispatcher lives in ContentCreator (`packages/ContextHub/packages/herdr/`), but this item is filed in SorraAgents and AC2/AC4 are SorraAgents-side.
- Answer (producer, 2026-11-18): "I don't think you are correct, I believe it's in the skill not the dispatcher. Correct me if I'm wrong. In the meantime do A." → **Option (a) SorraAgents-only.** Verification: the producer is correct — the dispatcher never commits; the observed commits are ad-hoc agent commits and the skill layer owns both the commit helpers and the guardrails. # Pre-commit hook guard sandbox tests

## Goal

As the implementer of the commit-time guard, I want a hermetic test that pins
exactly when `.githooks/pre-commit` must refuse and when it must stay silent, so
the guard can never regress into blocking legitimate work.

Test-first half of parent AC3. This item writes **tests only** — the hook itself
is the sibling item *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Context

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` is the sanctioned sandbox: `fixture_git_env()`,
  `scrub_repository_overrides()`, `run_git()`. It strips inherited `GIT_*`
  overrides so a polluted session environment cannot leak into the fixture.
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` is the precedent for a throw-away repo
  built from the committed `.githooks/` with `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` is the precedent for asserting the
  `scripts/install_pi.sh` wiring block itself.
- The guard target is narrow: **`dev` in the main checkout**. A linked worktree,
  a feature branch, `git merge --ff-only` and a `wl sync` commit must all pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new hermetic module `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` builds a
  throw-away repository from the committed `.githooks/` with
  `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, a bare local `origin` and a sandboxed `$HOME`; it
  never touches the real checkout, the real `$HOME` or the network.
- It asserts a commit on `dev` in the main checkout is **refused at commit time**:
  non-zero exit, `HEAD` unchanged, no new commit object, and the refusal message
  names the branch (`dev`), the main checkout path, the worktree requirement and
  the operator override.
- Zero-width proof: after the refused commit attempt the repository's commit
  count and `git rev-parse HEAD` are byte-identical to the pre-attempt values.
- It asserts the hook does **not** fire (exit 0, commit created) when:
  (a) the same commit runs inside a linked worktree (`git worktree add`);
  (b) the main checkout is on a feature branch;
  (c) `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` is set (and the override announces
  itself on stderr so a deliberate hot-fix stays auditable).
- It asserts the two legitimate main-checkout movements still succeed: a
  `git merge --ff-only` fast-forward of `dev` (no commit object is created) and a
  `wl sync`-style commit performed inside a temporary linked worktree
  (`.worklog/tmp-worktree-*`, detached `HEAD`) — the shape
  `ContextHub/dist/sync/worktree.js::withTempWorktree` uses.
- The suite is environment-clean: the fixture uses `fixture_git_env()` /
  `scrub_repository_overrides()` so inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` or
  `GIT_WORK_TREE` cannot influence a verdict.
- Tests are run only through the test skill (`run_tests.py`), never ad hoc; the
  new module passes once the hook item lands, and is red before it (the hook
  does not exist yet).

## Minimal implementation

- One test module, module-level docstring citing parent AC3 and the four
  negative cases, helper functions for "make a repo", "commit a file", "add a
  linked worktree".
- No production code, no changes to `.githooks/`, no changes to
  `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_pre_commit_main_checkout_guard.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)
- `tests/test_githooks_portability.py` (pattern to reuse)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Pre-commit hook refuses main-checkout dev commits*.

## Deliverables

- The failing-first test module and a short note on the red→green transition.

# Commit-helper guard tests for audit and code-review

## Goal

As a producer, I want the three skill commit helpers pinned by hermetic tests, so
"refuse to commit on `dev` in the main checkout" cannot be silently dropped from
one of them — especially from the duplicate `skill/code_review/` directory.

Test-first half of parent AC1. Tests only; the hardening is the sibling items
*Shared main-checkout commit guard + audit hardening* and *Harden code-review
commit helper in both directories*.

## Context

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_commit_config_remediation` (≈14222)
  stages one config file and commits with `REMEDIATION_COMMIT_MESSAGE`, locally,
  no push. Returns the short sha or `None`; its call site (≈14439) records
  failures into `results["chore_failures"]`.
- `skill/code-review/scripts/linter_runner.py::_commit_changes` (≈425) and the
  duplicate `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` (≈641) run `git add .`
  + `git commit -m "Auto-fix: <linter> applied fixes"`. Both directories are
  live: `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` and
  `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` import `code_review`; `code-review` is
  the skill-facing package that owns `SKILL.md`.
- The shared detection verdict must agree with `.githooks/pre-commit`:
  main checkout ⟺ `git rev-parse --git-dir` == `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`;
  target branch ⟺ `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` == `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hermetic tests (built on `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`) cover
  `_commit_config_remediation` and `_commit_changes` in both code-review
  directories.
- Refusal case: on `dev` in the main checkout the helper makes **no commit** and
  leaves **no staged change** behind (the staging step never runs), and returns
  its failure sentinel (`None` / `False`).
- Positive cases preserved: in a linked worktree, and on a feature branch in the
  main checkout, each helper still commits a real change — pinned for both.
- `ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT_DEV_COMMIT=1` makes every helper commit (consistent with
  the hook), and the override is logged so the deliberate act is traceable.
- Audit call site: a refusal is recorded in `results["chore_failures"]` with a
  message naming the worktree requirement and the work-item id, so the audit
  report states why the remediation was not committed — it is never silently
  dropped.

  drift apart again; an explicit assertion pins "both directories refuse
  identically".
- Unit tests for the new `skill/shared/commit_guard.py` detection helper
  (`is_main_checkout`, `current_branch`, `commit_refusal_reason`) cover the
  main-checkout, linked-worktree, feature-branch, detached-`HEAD` and override
  cases — so a shell and a Python verdict can never disagree.

## Minimal implementation

- One audit test module, one parametrised code-review test module, and one
  helper-unit test module (or a single module with three test classes).
- No production-code edits.

- `skill/audit/tests/` (new module for `_commit_config_remediation`)
- `skill/code-review/tests/` and/or `skill/code_review/tests/` (new parametrised module)
- `skill/shared/tests/` (new `test_commit_guard.py`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

- None. Must be merged before the two hardening items.

## Deliverables

- Red-first tests for all three helpers plus the shared guard primitive.

As a producer, when `implement.py start` refuses because `dev` is not a pushed
tip, I want the refusal pinned by tests that name the owning work items, so

  (≈8123-8137). `phase_start` (≈12081-12110) posts a work-item comment naming
  only the two tips, then releases the claim to `open`.
- `WORK_ITEM_ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}-[A-Z0-9]{2,})\b")` at
  `implement.py` ≈1951 is the existing id pattern — reuse it, do not add a

  that module rather than starting a new one.
- Related work: SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF (open) establishes that commit **body**
  mentions are not ownership evidence — AC2 says *subject scan*, so ownership is
  resolved from the subject only.

- `skill/implement/tests/test_start_base_resolution.py` gains tests asserting the

# Reconcile unpushed dev helper tests

## Goal

As a producer, I want the reconciliation helper's contract pinned by tests —
push by default, reset only on explicit confirmation — so recovery from a
poisoned `dev` can never destroy work by accident.

Test-first half of parent AC4. Tests only; the script and its documentation are
the sibling item *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

## Context

- The helper will live at `scripts/reconcile-unpushed-dev.sh` and is documented
  in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (pushed-tip guarantees section,
  ≈2638).
- Existing precedents for testing a repository script hermetically:
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`, `tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py`, and
  the sandbox helpers in `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`.
- Push policy: pushes go to `dev` only — never `main`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` builds a bare local `origin` plus
  a clone whose `dev` carries unpushed commits; no real checkout, `$HOME` or
  network is touched.
- Listing: output names each `origin/dev..dev` commit (short sha + subject) and
  its owning work item(s) parsed from the subject, with an explicit
  **unattributed** bucket.
- Default action is **push**: after a plain run, `origin/dev` advanced and local
  `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- Reset is opt-in only: without the explicit confirmation flag the helper refuses,
  mutates nothing (both refs byte-identical) and names the flag; with it, the
  helper prints the commits it discards **before** discarding, then resets so
  local `dev` equals `origin/dev`.
- No-op path: when `dev` == `origin/dev` the helper exits 0 with a clear "nothing
  to reconcile" message and mutates nothing.
- `--dry-run` lists and mutates nothing; `--json` emits a machine-readable
  document (commits, owning items, unattributed) stable enough for automation.
- Safety refusals: running in a linked worktree or with `dev` not checked out is
  refused with an actionable message (the helper targets the main checkout).
- Failure safety: a failed push leaves local `dev` unchanged and exits non-zero.

## Minimal implementation

- One hermetic test module driving the script through `subprocess` with a
  sandboxed environment and a local bare remote.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_reconcile_unpushed_dev.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (reused)

## Dependencies

- None. Must be merged before *Reconcile unpushed dev helper script and docs*.

- Red-first tests for the reconciliation helper.

# Parenthesise `render_summary()` list entries (ISC004 fix — Option A)

## Summary

Wrap the two multi-line f-string entries in `render_summary()`'s `lines` list in explicit parentheses, resolving both ruff ISC004 sites in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`. This is the producer-chosen Option A (fix in code) from the parent brief.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both live `ISC004` sites in `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` (`715-716` and `717-721`) are resolved so `ruff check --isolated --select ISC004 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` reports zero findings for the file.
2. The resolution survives line drift: the code no longer triggers the ISC004 rule, so no audit waiver is needed and no new ISC004 chore will be filed for this file after unrelated edits.
3. Rendered output is unchanged: the existing `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` tests for `render_summary()` pass unchanged, and at least one focused assertion covers the parenthesised form.
4. Sibling chores for the same two constructs (SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI line 712, SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ line 717) are cross-referenced and closed or superseded by this resolution — no duplicate work is performed.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs entries.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Implementation

In `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py`, the `render_summary()` function builds a `lines = [...]` list. The first two entries (the `window:` pair at lines 715-716 and the `corpus:` group at lines 717-721) use implicit string concatenation without surrounding parentheses.

**Change:** wrap each multi-line f-string entry in parentheses, matching the pattern already used in `render_checks()` (lines 700-708).

```python
# Before:
lines = [
    f"window: {report['window_start']} .. {report['window_end']} "
    f"(since post-fix {report['post_fix_commit']})",
    f"corpus: root={report['sessions_root']} "
    f"files_scanned={report['files_scanned']} "
    f"files_with_samples={report['files_with_samples']} "
    f"records_in_window={report['records_in_window']} "
    f"samples={report['total_samples']}",
]

# After:
lines = [
    (f"window: {report['window_start']} .. {report['window_end']} "
     f"(since post-fix {report['post_fix_commit']})"),
    (f"corpus: root={report['sessions_root']} "
     f"files_scanned={report['files_scanned']} "
     f"files_with_samples={report['files_with_samples']} "
     f"records_in_window={report['records_in_window']} "
     f"samples={report['total_samples']}"),
]
```

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — lines 715-721: wrap both list entries in parentheses.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — add a focused `render_summary()` test.

## Cross-references

Closes (supersedes): SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI, SA-0MWMOCFHU007PLOZ
Parent: SA-0MWMOCAIK001RKZ6

## Impact

Eliminates the ruff ISC004 false-positive noise on this small harness file with one behaviour-preserving edit.

## Goal

Red-first tests: pin the whole "never gate a tree you did not build" contract in
the existing `skill/implement` push-robustness harness **before** any production
change, so every later feature in this tree has a failing test to turn green.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC1a, AC1b, AC5, AC6, AC7).

## Scope

Tests only — no production change in this item. Extend the `sandbox` /
`_stubbed_finish` harness in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py`
(a scripted non-fast-forward recovery whose rebase introduces a new
`packages/shared` export while leaving `packages/shared/dist` stale) and, where
the assertion is cleaner at helper level, `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_retry.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test simulates a non-fast-forward rejection whose recovery rebase introduces a new `packages/shared` export and asserts (a) the build ran between the rebase and the retry push, and (b) the recorded push verdict is green/pushed.
- A test asserts the uncontended (no rejection) push path pays exactly one build per `finish`, and that the Step 3 changed-scope gate is never re-entered by the retry loop.
- A test asserts a failed post-rebase build produces no retry push, an actionable comment naming the build failure and the worktree, and the work item reset to `open`.
- A test asserts a stale-dist suite failure (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function` on a tree whose `packages/shared/dist` predates the rebase) is never reported as a failure of the pushed change set: the run either rebuilds first or fails closed with a build/resolution diagnosis naming the stale `packages/shared/dist`.
- Tests for every behaviour above are added to the `skill/implement` suite and pass, and the new tests fail against the pre-change implementation (no vacuous green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse the existing `sandbox` fixture and the `_stubbed_finish` monkeypatch seams; add one shared helper that scripts "rebase advances `dev` with a new shared export and leaves `dist` stale".
- Stub `run_build` / `git_push_to_dev` / `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` with call-order recording so "build between rebase and retry push" is asserted from the observed order, not from a mock's return value.
- Record the failing-red run evidence in a comment on this item (test names + the assertion each fails on).

## Key Files

## Goal

Backstop the rebuild: a finish run knows which tree it built, and a gate
failure whose symptom is a stale shared build is diagnosed as a
build/resolution problem naming `packages/shared/dist` — never attributed to
the pushed change set.

Parent: SA-0MWMRHW01009Q22Q (AC2, the hardening mechanism B).

## Scope

The built-tree marker + the stale-dist diagnosis. No change to the verdict
cache key (mechanism C is explicitly out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The finish run records the tree SHA (`HEAD^{tree}`) of the last successful build in the finish progress/report, and a HEAD tree that no longer matches it triggers a rebuild before any dev push — including the retry push — so no push ever gates an unbuilt tree; when that rebuild itself fails the run fails closed with a stale-build diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`.
- A gate failure whose symptom is a stale shared build (`TypeError: <new export> is not a function`, which the existing load-flake retry does not match because the module loads fine) is reported as a build/resolution diagnosis naming `packages/shared/dist`, never as a failure of the pushed change set.
- The guard adds no build on a tree that has not changed since the last build, and the changed-scope gate (Step 3) is never re-entered.
- Tests cover the stale-tree trigger, the unchanged-tree no-op, and the diagnosis wording.

## Minimal Implementation

- Record the built tree SHA via `_set_finish_progress` (an existing field surface — no new file format) when `run_build` succeeds in Step 2 and after the post-rebase rebuild.
- Before a dev push, compare `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` with the recorded value in the worktree; on mismatch rebuild (reusing `run_build`) and update the marker, or fail closed with the diagnosis when the rebuild fails.
- Classify a gate failure whose stderr tail matches the stale-shared symptom (`TypeError: <identifier> is not a function` where the identifier resolves from `packages/shared`) into the existing build/resolution diagnosis taxonomy instead of a change-set failure.
- Keep `_is_gate_load_flake` unchanged — this is a distinct symptom, not a load error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_set_finish_progress` (~759), `run_build` (~9324), `_is_gate_load_flake` (~6032), the push loop and gate-failure classification (~13560–13890).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_provenance.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_push_robustness.py` — provenance + push-robustness tests.

## Deliverables

The built-tree marker, the freshness check, the stale-dist diagnosis, and tests.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Rebuild the rebased worktree before the retry push" (shares the post-rebase rebuild surface).

## Goal

Red-first regression coverage for the drive pre-spawn model validation path: a permanently-unresolvable model pattern must fail fast with an actionable message and consume **no** infrastructure retries.

User story: As the agent implementing this epic, I want the fast-fail behaviour pinned by failing-first tests, so the implementation in F3/F4 is driven by an executable specification rather than prose.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. Sibling F2 covers the spawn-argv assertions; F3/F4 land the implementation. Today `_default_session_spawner` spawns `pi -p "/skill:implement <child>" --approve --no-extensions` with **no** explicit model, `classify_spawn_failure` classifies the resulting `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` stderr as `infrastructure`, and `phase_drive` burns five retries (`--infra-retry-limit`, backoff `[2, 4, 8, 16, 30]`) before stopping.

Empirical facts to encode in the tests (verified on this machine):

- `pi -p … --model "MunitoAI/*"` exits **1** and writes to stderr: `Warning: No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`, `Warning: Model "*" not found for provider "MunitoAI". Using custom model id.`, then a `404 … "code": "model_not_found"` line.
- `pi --list-models` exits **0** and prints a fixed-width `provider  model  context  max-out  thinking  images` table (the authoritative available-model catalogue).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test drives the spawn-argument / pre-spawn validation path with an unresolvable pattern and asserts the fast-fail message and that no infra retries are consumed.
- The same test asserts no child session is spawned (spawner call count is zero) and `infra_retries` stays empty, so the failure is charged to nothing.
- The fast-fail message under test names both the unresolvable pattern and the available providers.
- Catalogue parsing is unit-tested from a captured `pi --list-models` fixture, with no subprocess and no reliance on the host's model configuration.
- Tests are written first and observed red against the current code, then green after F3/F4 (the red observation is recorded in a comment on this item).
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (or `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` when they exercise the retry accounting) and use the existing fake-spawner harness.

## Implementation sketch

1. Capture a `pi --list-models` sample as a test fixture string (Local Proxy / deepseek / MunitoAI rows plus the `No models match pattern` warning line).
2. Write the fast-fail test: patch the spawner, run `phase_drive`/the pre-flight entry point with an unresolvable pattern, assert the refusal message, `sessions_spawned == 0`, and the infra-retry counter untouched.
3. Write the catalogue-parse and resolution-precedence unit tests (they will reference the helpers F3 introduces — coordinate the helper names with F3 before merging).

## Constraints

- Tests must not shell out to `pi` or read the host's `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; everything is injected via fixtures and monkeypatched spawners.
- No new test-only seams in production code beyond what F3/F4 already introduce.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

## Impact

Nothing user-visible on its own; it is the executable specification that keeps a stalled drive from silently regressing to five retries.

## Goal

Red-first regression coverage that pins the exact child-session argv for **both** drive transports: a resolvable model must produce an argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete `provider/model`.

User story: As the agent implementing this epic, I want both spawners' argv pinned by tests, so a future refactor cannot silently drop the explicit model and reintroduce the headless default-resolution defect.

## Context

Parent: SA-0MWOUI3Q0006TTSY. F1 covers the fast-fail/pre-validation tests; F4 implements the argv change.

The two spawn paths are:

- Headless (`_default_session_spawner`): `[pi_bin, "-p", "/skill:implement <child>", "--approve", "--no-extensions"]`.
- Pane (`_pane_session_spawner`, opt-in via `--pane-sessions`): `herdr agent start <agent> --kind pi --pane <id> -- --approve --no-extensions`.

Neither passes `--provider`/`--model` today, so the child inherits the machine's default model selection — which resolves the unservable `MunitoAI/*` glob on the affected machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test asserts that a resolvable pattern still produces a correct argv that explicitly names the resolved concrete model (`--provider <provider> --model <model>`) for the headless `pi -p` spawner.
- An equivalent test pins the pane spawner argv: the resolved `--provider`/`--model` pair is present in the `herdr agent start … -- <args>` argument list, alongside the existing `--approve --no-extensions`.
- The pane-transport test asserts `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` is unchanged and no model/credential material is added to the pane environment (authority stays in argv, not env).
- A test asserts the child argv carries a concrete pair with no glob or wildcard characters (`*`, `?`), so a pattern can never be forwarded literally.
- Tests are written first, observed red against the current spawners, and green after F4 (the red observation is recorded in a comment on this item).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extend the existing spawner tests to capture `cmd` via a monkeypatched `subprocess.run` (headless) and a fake herdr client (pane).
2. Assert the model flags and their order/value; assert absence of wildcards.
3. Add the pane env invariant assertion.

## Constraints

- No live `pi`/`herdr` invocation: both transports are exercised with fakes only.
- Assert on argv contents, not on log output.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_child_session.py`
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`

## Impact

Nothing user-visible on its own; it locks the fix at the argv level so a driven child session can never again start on an unservable default model.

# Provision vendored `node_modules` in audit worktrees

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

The audit creates two throwaway worktrees — the F3 **execution** worktree
(`<host>/.worklog/worktrees/audit-exec-<id>`, `_create_execution_worktree`) and the
merge-gate **integration** worktree (`audit-merge-<id>`, `_integrate_into_dev`).
Both initialise git submodules and symlink the **root** `node_modules` only. A repo
that vendors a pi package under `.pi/packages/<pkg>/` with its own gitignored
`node_modules` therefore has an unresolvable dependency graph inside the worktree
while the populated checkout resolves it fine (observed: ContentCreator
`tests/test_rebuild_wiki_meta.py`, `Cannot find package 'mdast-util-from-markdown'`).

`implement.py` already solves this for implement worktrees
(`_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`). The audit has no equivalent, and there
must be **one** provisioner, not a second copy.

## Scope

- Promote the nested-`node_modules` discovery + symlink logic into a shared module.
- Call it from both audit worktree creation sites, after submodule initialisation
  and before the build/suite runs.
- Emit evidence lines so a reviewer can see what was provisioned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC1 — The audit F3 execution worktree (single-stage and the two-stage pinned/merge-gate variant) provides **every** vendored dependency tree the suite needs — e.g. initialise submodules, then link or bootstrap both the root `node_modules` **and** each `.pi/packages/*/node_modules` (or run the project's own bootstrap/install step).
- [ ] One shared provisioner (`skill/shared/worktree_deps.py`) discovers nested `node_modules` directories under a checkout root and symlinks each into the worktree, never overwriting an existing entry and never fabricating a package directory the worktree lacks.
- [ ] `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` keeps `_iter_nested_node_modules` / `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` as delegating wrappers, so its existing call sites and patched tests are unchanged.
- [ ] Both `_create_execution_worktree` (F3 execution worktree) and `_integrate_into_dev` (merge-gate worktree) provision nested `node_modules` after `_ensure_worktree_submodules` and before the build/suite, appending greppable evidence (`nested node_modules provisioned: <n> (<paths>)`, or a best-effort failure note).
- [ ] Provisioning is best-effort: a failure records evidence and never aborts the audit or fails the merge gate.
- [ ] Unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` cover discovery pruning (`.git`/`.worklog`/`node_modules` never descended, symlinked dirs never followed, root `node_modules` excluded), symlink creation, no-overwrite, missing-parent skip, and per-candidate failure tolerance — with no suite execution.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Move `_NESTED_NODE_MODULES_PRUNE_DIRS`, `_iter_nested_node_modules` and `_ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks` into `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (public names `iter_nested_node_modules`, `ensure_nested_node_modules_symlinks`).
2. Re-export them from `implement.py` as thin wrappers preserving the current return types and log lines.
3. Add `_provision_worktree_dependencies(worktree_path, host_root) -> list[str]` in `audit_runner.py`: the existing root `node_modules` symlink plus the nested symlinks, returning evidence lines.
4. Call it from `_create_execution_worktree` (after submodules, replacing the inline symlink block) and from `_integrate_into_dev` (same point in the integration sequence).
5. Add `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` — written red-first.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_worktree_deps.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` (existing merge-gate coverage to extend)

## Constraints

- Fail-open, mirroring `_ensure_worktree_submodules`: never a new hard dependency of the audit.
- Symlinks only: never copy, never install, never invoke a package manager inside a worktree (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B convention).
- Preserve the ordering hazard fix: submodules → dependency provisioning → build/suite (SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ).
- Cross-repo `--code-root` hosting of the merge-gate worktree is **out of scope** (execution-worktree hosting was SA-0MWO59J9T002IQ63); this slice provisions from the root each site already uses.

## Impact

Suites in the audit's throwaway worktrees resolve the same dependency graph as the real checkout, so vendored-package tests stop failing for environmental reasons.
data.title: Provision vendored node_modules in audit worktrees

# Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure

**Parent:** SA-0MWQZGZ83001RSO6 (Audit F3 execution worktree misses vendored `.pi/packages/*/node_modules`)

## Problem

`_run_tests_via_test_skill` triages every parsed failure **before** the red-suite
mode evaluation runs, so a failure caused by the audit worktree's own missing
dependency still mints a critical `test-failure` child on the audited item
(WL-0MWQXIR2J0001E1A in the observed incident). The consequence: a complete epic
reads "Ready to close: No" and needs producer review to delete a phantom blocker.

A suppression contract already exists for verdicts that must never mint an item —
`detect_phantom` / `PHANTOM_NOTICE_CODES` for `state_changed_during_run`
(WL-0MVSPZ1FH000RWET). This slice adds the infrastructure case alongside it.

## Scope

- Evidence-based detector: a module-resolution failure whose importer path resolves
  inside the audit execution worktree **and** whose named dependency exists in the
  populated checkout.
- Audit runner: suppress those failures from triage (before any `wl` mutation) and
  report them.
- Triage helper: honour an explicit infrastructure signal so no caller can mint an
  item from it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Covers parent AC3 — Suite failures whose evidence is a missing/absent dependency inside the audit worktree are classified as **infrastructure**, not product failures: they never create `test-failure` work items and never leave the audited item blocked by an auto-created child.
- [ ] Detection is conservative and evidence-based: a missing-module/package failure is infrastructure only when the failing importer path resolves inside the audit execution worktree AND the named dependency is present in the populated checkout; a genuinely missing product dependency stays a product failure.
- [ ] The audit runner skips triage for infrastructure failures before any `wl` mutation (no `check_or_create` call, no dependency wiring) and records them in a `suppressed_infrastructure` result key plus the run summary line and gate evidence.
- [ ] `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` suppresses on the explicit signal (`notice_code: missing_dependency_in_worktree` or `infrastructure: true`) exactly as it does for phantoms, returning `suppressed: true` without a lookup or creation.
- [ ] Infrastructure failures never upgrade an execution-dependent AC to `met`: no green evidence means the AC stays `partial` (the runner's fail-closed evidence invariant is preserved).
- [ ] Unit tests pin detection positives and negatives plus both suppression paths (audit runner and triage helper) without executing a suite.

## Minimal Implementation

1. `skill/shared/test_infra.py`: `INFRA_NOTICE_CODE`, `detect_missing_dependency(text)` (Node `Cannot find module/package`, `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, Python `ModuleNotFoundError`, TS2307) and `classify_infrastructure_failure(failure, *, worktree_root, main_checkout_root)` returning `None` unless environment causality is proven.
2. `audit_runner.py`: partition `failures` before the triage loop so only product failures reach `check_or_create`; add `suppressed_infrastructure` to the returned dict and the `Test skill run completed:` summary line; surface the count in the evidence block.
3. `triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`: `detect_infrastructure(payload)` checked after `detect_phantom`, returning the same suppressed shape (no lookup, no creation, no dependency edge).
4. Tests: `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py`, `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py`, and an audit-runner test asserting zero triage calls for an infrastructure failure record.

## Key Files

- `skill/shared/test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/shared/tests/test_test_infra.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `skill/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py`
- `skill/triage/tests/test_check_or_create_infrastructure.py` (new)

## Constraints

- No inferred similarity: suppression fires only on evidence proving environment causality, so a genuine failure on a stable checkout is never swallowed.
- Never suppress a failure whose evidence does not name a missing module/package.
- Do not widen this into "excuse every unrelated failure": that ordering question is separate and out of scope.

## Impact

A missing vendored dependency inside the audit worktree can no longer create a phantom high-priority `test-failure` blocker on the audited item.
data.title: Classify audit-worktree dependency failures as infrastructure

# Driven child in a foreign-project worktree cannot resolve its owning worklog store

> **Re-filed from `WL-0MWR2YY26002T6ZD` (ContextHub) on 2026-11-22.** The
> failing code lives in the **SorraAgents** skill tree
> (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `_child_session_env` /
> `resolve_worklog_dir`), and this is the same store-resolution family as
> SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51, SA-0MWC6S0TY007I45U and SA-0MUDYLNY600609WG. Original
> provenance and intake brief preserved below.

## Problem statement

When `implement.py drive` drives a work item whose owning store belongs to a
*different* project from the repository the worktree is created in (a `WL-`
item hosted in ContextHub but driven from a SorraAgents worktree, or the mirror
case), the driven child session runs with `cwd` inside a worktree that carries
that repository's repo-tracked `.worklog/config.yaml` (e.g. `prefix: SA`). A
plain `wl` call therefore resolves the **host repository's** store and reports
the child's own `WL-` item as "not found", so the child can neither claim, read
nor comment on its own work item and exits without producing work — and may
silently create a throwaway `worktree/.worklog/worklog.db` against the wrong
store.

## Users

- **Downtime dispatcher / driving agent** — wants `/skill:implement drive` to
  run any work item regardless of which project hosts its store, without
  caller-side shims.
- **Producer** — wants multi-hour cross-project epics to be drivable through
  the sanctioned `drive` transport instead of a manual interactive session.
- **Maintainer of the worklog stores** — wants a foreign child to write to its
  own store and never to a spurious worktree-scoped database.

Example user stories:

- *As a driving agent, I want a driven child for a `WL-` item to resolve the
  ContextHub store even when its worktree lives under SorraAgents, so it can
  claim/read/comment/finish its own item without a PATH shim.*
- *As a maintainer, I want a driven child of the host repository's own prefix
  (`SA-`) to keep resolving the SorraAgents store, so same-project epics are
  unaffected.*
- *As a producer, I want the store-resolution precedence (flag > env > cwd) to
  be documented and tested, so I can reason about which store a command hits.*

## Impact

Cross-project work items become drivable through `implement.py drive` without a
caller-side PATH shim, so a driven child works its own store instead of silently
mutating a throwaway database in the worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A driven child for a foreign-prefix work item (a `WL-` item whose source
  lives in the SorraAgents checkout) resolves its **owning** store
  (ContextHub `.worklog`) and can claim, read, comment and finish without any
  caller-side shim or PATH wrapper.
- A driven child for the repository's own prefix (`SA-`) keeps resolving the
  repository's store — no regression for same-project epics.
- `wl` (ContextHub CLI) honours the resolved store via an environment variable,
  with a documented precedence rule **flag > env > cwd** (the `--worklog-dir`
  flag always wins, then the env var, then cwd-based resolution).
- `implement.py`'s `_child_session_env` exports the store resolved **for that
  specific child id** (reusing `resolve_worklog_dir(child_id)`), so a
  cross-project child resolves its own store while a same-project child keeps
  the repository default.
- `wl sync` semantics from a worktree are unchanged (still refused /
  main-checkout-only) and no throwaway `worktree/.worklog/worklog.db` is
  created in a foreign worktree.
- Tests cover the precedence rule (flag > env > cwd) in both repositories and
  the cross-project driven-child end-to-end path.
- At least one testing/validation criterion is satisfied by an automated test.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Two-repository change.** The `wl` CLI lives in ContextHub
  (`src/worklog-paths.ts`, `src/cli.ts`/`src/cli-main.ts`); the driven-child
  environment is built in SorraAgents
  (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`, `_child_session_env`). Both sides
  are required for the end-to-end fix.
- **Precedence is a public contract.** `--worklog-dir` must continue to
  override everything; the new env fallback sits between the flag and cwd. This
  rule must be documented and tested so `wl sync` from a worktree is unaffected.
- **Existing `resolve_worklog_dir`** (SorraAgents `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  already does prefix-to-sibling resolution and must be reused rather than
  re-implemented.
- **`wl sync` is main-checkout-only** and its refusal semantics must not
  regress; no second store/DB may be created inside a managed worktree.
- **No caller-side shims.** The interim PATH shim used to unblock the epic is
  explicitly *not* part of the fix.
- **Env-var naming.** `generate_standup.py` already honours `WL_WORKLOG_DIR`,
  while herdr's `claim-lock.ts` honours `WORKLOG_DIR`. The chosen name must be
  documented; alignment between the two conventions is preferred over adding a
  third.

## Existing state

- `implement.py start <WL-id>` from `cwd=SorraAgents` succeeds: it resolves the
  store by **prefix-to-sibling scan** and creates
  `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-…`.
- The driven child then runs (per session log) `cd .../SorraAgents && wl show
  WL-…` → *"The work-item … does not exist in the worklog database"*, and greps
  the SA `worklog-data.jsonl` instead.
- `wl --worklog-dir /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/.worklog show WL-…`
  works, but the CLI has **no env-var equivalent** for `--worklog-dir`
  (`WL_WORKLOG_DIR` is only honoured by skill scripts such as
  `generate_standup.py`), so `implement.py` cannot hand the resolved store to
  the child through the environment today.
- The child also writes a throwaway `worktree/.worklog/worklog.db` (SA store)
  on its first `wl` mutation, so the failure is silent-ish: it mutates the
  wrong store.
- `_child_session_env` currently injects only `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_RECURSION`,
  the lock-ownership token, and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`; it exports no store
  pointer.

## Desired change

Chosen approach (see Appendix — **OPEN QUESTION**, recommendation **(A)**):

**(A) `wl` honours the env var as the `--worklog-dir` fallback.** In
ContextHub, `resolveWorklogDir()`/`setWorklogDirOverride`/argv parsing gains an
env fallback ordered **flag > env > cwd**. In SorraAgents, `_child_session_env`
exports the store resolved **for the child's id** (via
`resolve_worklog_dir(child_id)`), so a foreign child resolves its own store
while a same-project child keeps the repo default. Documented precedence rule
and tests in both repositories.

Alternatives (recorded, not recommended):

- **(B) Per-worktree store pointer.** `phase_start` writes an untracked
  `.worklog` pointer/symlink for foreign-prefix items; `cleanup`/`abort`
  removes it. SorraAgents-only, but adds filesystem magic inside the worktree
  and risks the foreign-change-surface guard seeing an unexpected path.
- **(C) Document a manual fallback only.** Cross-project items are implemented
  by a single interactive session that passes `--worklog-dir` explicitly; no
  `drive`. Does not fix the reported failure.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — env var leaking into unrelated `wl` invocations.** An exported
  `WL_WORKLOG_DIR`/`WORKLOG_DIR` is inherited by the whole child session, so a
  later `wl sync` (or any `wl` command) would also target the foreign store.
  Mitigation: `wl sync` must keep its main-checkout-only refusal (it already
  cross-checks the resolved store against the cwd repo — see
  `src/sync/repo-context.ts`), and the precedence rule must be covered by a
  test proving `wl sync` still refuses from a foreign worktree. Scope the env
  var to store *resolution* only; do not change `wl sync` semantics.
- **Risk — two naming conventions** (`WL_WORKLOG_DIR` in `generate_standup.py`
  vs `WORKLOG_DIR` in herdr `claim-lock.ts`). Mitigation: document the chosen
  name (assumption: prefer aligning on one existing convention rather than
  adding a third).
- **Risk — cross-repo coordination.** The fix spans ContextHub and SorraAgents,
  so a change in one without the other leaves the failure (half-fix). The
  acceptance criteria require end-to-end evidence.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Adjacent opportunities (e.g. a general worktree
  store-pointer, or unifying the two env conventions) are recorded as linked
  work items rather than folded into this fix.
- **Assumption —** the interim PATH shim is retired once this lands; it is not
  part of the deliverable.
- **Assumption —** `resolve_worklog_dir(child_id)` is authoritative for
  prefix-to-sibling resolution and needs no behavioural change.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/worklog-paths.ts` — add the env-var fallback to
  `resolveWorklogDir()`/`setWorklogDirOverride`/argv parsing, ordered
  flag > env > cwd.
- `src/cli-main.ts`, `src/cli.ts` — wire the env fallback before any resolution
  happens (mirroring the existing `--worklog-dir` early-apply path).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_session_env` exports the
  store resolved for the child id; the `phase_drive` call site passes the
  resolved store or child id.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reuse the existing `resolve_worklog_dir`
  for per-child resolution (no new resolver).
- Tests: ContextHub `tests/…` (precedence flag > env > cwd) and SorraAgents
  `skill/implement/tests/…` (cross-project child env carries the right store).

## Related work

- Discovered-from: **WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC** (guarded main-checkout verdict epic)
  — no blocking edge; the epic proceeds with the interim caller-side shim and
  this item is the durable fix.
- Evidence session: **WL-0MWR1OUF7009FG4I** (2026-11-22, test-main-checkout
  churn verdict pins).
- Older occurrence: worktree
  `wl-WL-0MV981ZGA007ARPG-regression-tests-concurrent-dev-origin-r` (2026-10-17).
- Adjacent prior work (cross-repo dependencies, foreign blockers): WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD,
  WL-0MVWEEQ8K0013DOY, WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC — these cover *dependency-edge*
  resolution, not driven-child store resolution, so they are related context,
  not duplicates.
- `generate_standup.py` — existing `WL_WORKLOG_DIR` convention; herdr
  `claim-lock.ts` — existing `WORKLOG_DIR` convention.
- **Same family in this store:** SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 (shared skill scripts
  resolve the wrong store), SA-0MWC6TEBY009YLST / SA-0MWC6S0TY007I45U
  (`filing_location.py` helper), SA-0MUDYLNY600609WG (validate filing location
  during intake) — related store-resolution context, not duplicates.
- Cross-project reference (ContextHub): WL-0MWFKDFFA009N3OC (discovered-from),
  WL-0MWR1OUF7009FG4I (evidence session).

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by the find-related skill (`--work-item-id WL-0MWR2YY26002T6ZD`,
run while filed in ContextHub); full report at
`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MWR2YY26002T6ZD.md` in the ContextHub
checkout.

### Related work items

- **WL-0MVXY2N0Y008ICLW** – Close coverage gap: runs where the coordination
  dir cannot be resolved degrade exactly as today (completed).
- **WL-0MS99Y6R40028Q9G** – `wl sync` in a git worktree commits the whole tree
  as deleted (data loss) (completed) — directly relevant to the "`wl sync` from
  a worktree stays unchanged" constraint.
- **WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ** – `wl audit-set` should fail hard when audit text is
  not persisted (completed).

### Repository file matches

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — drive/claim/lock/dispatch context.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` and `CLI.md` — CLI and herdr store-resolution
  context.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — Which proposed fix should be implemented?

The work item says "Proposed fixes (pick one at intake)". The choice materially
changes the implementation, so it must not be auto-selected.

- **(A) `wl` env fallback + driver exports the per-child store** — documented
  flag > env > cwd precedence; cross-repo change; testable end-to-end.
- **(B) Per-worktree store pointer** — SorraAgents-only; filesystem magic in
  the worktree; risk to the foreign-change-surface guard.
- **(C) Document a manual fallback only** — no `drive`; does not fix the
  failure.

**Recommended:** (A) — it fixes the reported failure end-to-end with a small,
documented, testable precedence rule and no filesystem magic, and it reuses the
existing `resolve_worklog_dir` resolver.

- **Answer:** _OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer/producer-agent decision._
- **Source:** pending producer review (`wl reviewed … true`).

## Goal

Test-first slice for SA-0MWRCSJK8000H9HA: pin the **guard-level** contract of
`implement._child_main_checkout_violation` so that main-checkout dirt is
reported even when the child's worktree also holds work, while every existing
exemption survives. No production code changes in this item.

## Context

Today the function returns `None` as soon as the child's worktree holds any
change (`_git_path_has_changes`: dirty files or commits ahead of the parent
branch), so the main checkout is never inspected — the 2026-11-22 incident
shape (an abandoned main-checkout edit plus a committed slice in the worktree).
`phase_parent`'s two call sites also only invoke the guard when the worktree is
clean, so the gap is invisible at parent/drive level too.

## Required expectations

Each row is one test (real git sandboxes via `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, the
convention used by `test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — never re-implement
the guard):

| # | Child worktree | Main checkout | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | commits ahead of `dev` | tracked file modified | violation naming that path |
| 2 | uncommitted dirty file | tracked file modified | violation naming that path |
| 3 | commits ahead of `dev` | clean | `None` |
| 4 | commits ahead of `dev` | `.worklog/`-only dirt | `None` |
| 5 | commits ahead of `dev` | project-declared `ignoreDirtyPaths` dirt only | `None` |
| 6 | commits ahead of `dev` | modified file | spawn-failure evidence recorded → `None` |
| 7 | behind-only (no dirty files, no commits ahead) | modified file | violation (the worktree holds no work) |
| 8 | commits ahead of `dev` | sibling worktree dirty | `None` (sibling exemption unchanged) |

Plus one end-to-end `phase_parent` case (harness pattern of
`test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py::_run_phase_parent`): child worktree with
commits, main checkout dirty → `success: False`, `placement_violation: True`,
`next_child` set, offending path in the message, **no** `StatusLifecycle`
status write and **no** `finish`/`start` subprocess invocation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new test module exercises the eight-row matrix above against the production
  `_child_main_checkout_violation` with real git sandboxes.
- The end-to-end `phase_parent` case asserts `success: False`,
  `placement_violation: True`, the offending path in `report["message"]`, an
  empty `update_status` call list and no invoked subprocess.
- The new expectations are `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` (the repo's
  test-first convention) so the suite stays green before the fix, and the
  module reports exactly the expected xfail count with no unexpected passes.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is not modified by this item.
- The module passes unchanged (with markers removed by the implementing
  sibling) as the verification target for the fix item.
- The same violation is detected by `_child_main_checkout_violation` when called from `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` (the parent/drive placement guard).
- The violation occurs even when the child's worktree also has commits ahead of the parent branch (the current gap: condition 3 is treated as a complete exemption).
- Pre-existing, unrelated dirt in the main checkout (unattributed to the child) is still handled correctly — the fix must not regress the existing exemption for ambient dirt when the worktree is the only change surface.
- Validation: the new behaviour is demonstrated by tests that fail before the fix and pass after it (guard-level).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_placement_guard_dirty_main_checkout.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` (fixture and harness conventions to mirror)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (real git sandbox helpers)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (read-only reference: `_child_main_checkout_violation`, `_git_path_has_changes`, `record_spawn_failure`)

## Minimal implementation

- Add the module with the eight-row matrix plus the `phase_parent` end-to-end
  case (real git sandboxes, `xfail(strict=True)` markers).
- Run the module through the test skill and record the xfail count in the item
  comment.

## Out of scope

The fix itself, the finish gate, docs. No behaviour change lands here.

## Goal

Test-first slice for SA-0MWRCSJK8000H9HA: pin the **finish-gate** contract so
`implement.py finish` refuses — with an actionable, path-naming message — when
the child's worktree holds its work and the main checkout also holds dirt, even
though `cwd` is inside the worktree. No production code changes in this item.

## Context

`_worktree_placement_violation` returns `None` immediately when `cwd` is the
worktree or inside it (condition 1), and again when the worktree holds changes
(condition 3). A driven child finishes from inside its worktree, so the finish
placement gate currently never sees main-checkout dirt on the normal path —
AC1/AC3 of the parent item cannot be met without changing both.

## Required expectations

| # | cwd | Child worktree | Main checkout | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | inside the worktree | commits ahead of `dev` | tracked file modified | violation naming the path and the worktree |
| 2 | inside the worktree | uncommitted dirty file | tracked file modified | violation |
| 3 | inside the worktree | commits ahead of `dev` | clean | `None` |
| 4 | inside the worktree | commits ahead of `dev` | `.worklog/`-only and declared expected-dirty dirt | `None` |

The headline case is the incident shape (parent AC4): a **fake child** whose
session writes an **absolute path under the main checkout** — the
`cd <main-checkout> && printf … > /abs/path` form, not a path relative to its
own worktree — and then finishes from inside its worktree. The test models the
write with `Path(main / "tests" / "helpers" / "fake-tools.ts").write_text(...)`
and asserts the refusal names that absolute path.

Plus `phase_finish` behaviour through a harness modelled on
`test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py::_finish_harness` (that harness stubs the
placement gate, so this test patches only the other boundaries): the run returns
`success: False`, `worktree_enforcement`-style placement reporting,
`report["steps"]["worktree_placement"] == {"success": False, "reason": "placement_violation"}`,
the work item is released to `open` (never `completed`/`in_review`), and a
`wl` comment carries the offending paths. A clean main checkout in the same
harness reaches the terminal transition (no regression).

Message contract (AC5): the refusal names every offending path, names the
worktree, tells the agent to **move** the edit into the worktree (or discard
it), and explains the rule — every write path must resolve inside the worktree,
`cwd` alone is not sufficient.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new test module exercises the four-row matrix above against the production
  `_worktree_placement_violation`.
- The absolute-path case (a fake child writing under the main checkout, then
  finishing from its worktree) is refused with a placement violation naming the
  written path.
- A `phase_finish` case asserts `success: False`, the structured
  `steps.worktree_placement` entry, the work item released to `open`, and that
  the posted comment contains the offending path.
- The message assertion pins the recovery instruction ("move" + worktree path)
  and the `cwd`-is-not-sufficient rule.
- A clean-main-checkout case reaches the terminal transition (no regression for
  a legitimate finish).
- The new expectations are `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)`; the module reports
  the expected xfail count with no unexpected passes.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is not modified by this item.
- A driven child that leaves the main checkout dirty at a path inside the repo fails its `finish` with a placement-violation refusal, naming the offending paths.
- Covered by a test: a fake child that writes an absolute path under the main checkout is refused at `finish` with a placement violation.
- The failure message tells the agent to move the edit into the worktree and explains the rule (work must be inside the worktree, not in `cwd` alone).
- Validation: the new behaviour is demonstrated by tests that fail before the fix and pass after it (finish-gate level).

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_placement_dirty_main_checkout.py` (new)
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_guard.py` (finish harness pattern)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (real git sandbox helpers)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (read-only reference: `_worktree_placement_violation`, `phase_finish` Step 0.5)

## Minimal implementation

- Add the module with the four-row matrix, the absolute-path fake-child case
  and the `phase_finish` refusal/no-regression cases (`xfail(strict=True)`).
- Run the module through the test skill and record the xfail count in the item
  comment.

## Out of scope

The fix itself, the parent/drive guard, docs.

discovered-from:LP-0MWLZ68SF0052E7Z

# Finding

A `implement.py finish` in one item's worktree was failed by the **pre-lock dev-push full-suite
gate** with `reason: full_suite_red`, `failure_kind: infrastructure`, even though the suite passed:

```
Dev-push full-suite verdict is RED for tree d245c11691cee7761d3d5f18f685290b93863843
(reason: infrastructure). Resolved before the finish lock was taken, so nothing was
committed or pushed and local dev was not advanced.
No structured test failures were parsed.
Live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for
.../wl-LP-0MWLZ68SF0052E7Z-... in main checkout /home/rgardler/projects/llm:
  added path [??] .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_prefill_eta_pricing_basis.py
  added path [??] proxy/tests/test_local_admission_stamp_consistency.py
  added path [??] proxy/tests/test_measured_basis_eta_pricing.py
```

Facts:

- Suite result: **1208 passed, 2 skipped in 35.7 s** (plus the hidden skill suite); no test failures.
- The three untracked paths are **not** in the finishing item's change set (docs + one new script +
  its test). They are test files another, concurrent herdr-driven implement session was authoring in
  the **main checkout**; they had vanished by the time the gate reported. Main-checkout `HEAD` was
  also advanced by that session (`33193b28c` → `bedbb57c6`) during the run.
- Consequence: item released to `open`, ~10 min of suite work discarded, and a retry was needed.
  The retry (after fast-forwarding the worktree onto the newer `dev`) succeeded and — correctly, by
  design — served the green from the **change-set** cache for the identical patch.

This is the third recorded occurrence: LP-0MVVXGLTM008ROJ9 (`LP-0MWL4O2Z1007KAG4`) and
LP-0MVZF4SU10032OZH (`LP-0MWJUVZKY001Z442`) recorded the same shape, both as **record-only** chores
(i.e. the block was documented and resolved by waiting, never fixed). Earlier guard work
(SA-0MVWMUBP10041CSM, SA-0MVXVESV5002HWTW, SA-0MVXPPN22001FS5L, SA-0MV0EFEAB006X79B,
SA-0MV8311B3005DNG8) addressed cross-checkout attribution, `wl sync` churn and ownership exclusion;
foreign **untracked file creation in the main checkout during the suite** still fails an unrelated
item's finish.

# Goal

As an agent finishing a work item, I want a concurrent session's transient churn in the main
checkout to be excluded from (or re-baselined out of) my gate verdict, so a green suite is not
discarded because somebody else was authoring files — while the guard keeps failing on *my* own
mutation and on any mutation the suite itself causes in a guarded checkout.

# Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Foreign churn cannot fail the verdict.** A run whose diff-versus-baseline consists only of
  paths outside the finishing item's change set (not in its would-be-commit tree, not owned by its
  worktree) reports the suite's real verdict; those paths are recorded as
  `foreign_churn_excluded` evidence instead of `full_suite_red`/`infrastructure`.
- **AC2 — Guard still fails closed on real mutations.** The verdict is still red when (a) a path in
  the item's own change set is mutated after the baseline, or (b) the suite mutates a guarded
  checkout, or (c) the baseline cannot be established — each with a named reason.
- **AC3 — Regression tests.** A test drives a finish/suite run while a *foreign* writer creates and
  removes an untracked file in the main checkout and asserts the run completes with the suite's
  verdict; a paired test asserts the item's own late mutation still fails. No real sleeps: use the
  existing hook/fixture seams.
- **AC4 — Actionable message.** When the gate does fail on churn, the message names the owning
  item/worktree/session when determinable, so the operator can see whose work caused it (today it
  names only the finishing item).
- **AC5 — Suite + docs.** Full suite green through the test skill; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` (or the
  guard's own doc) states the foreign-churn rule.

# Notes

- Not to be confused with the *change-set cache* behaviour seen on the retry (a rebased,
  patch-identical push serving a green verdict): that is intended (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC), but it does
  mean the **pushed tree** was never itself full-suite-tested — worth stating in the doc alongside
  AC5.
- Root cause candidates to check first: the baseline is captured on the *main checkout* while the
  change set lives in a *linked worktree*, so "paths absent from the baseline" and "paths not in the
  item's tree" are conflated; ownership exclusion may only apply to paths the runner knows about
  (`git_sandbox`), not to untracked creations in the shared checkout.

# Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (pre-lock full-suite verdict, `main_checkout_guard`,
  `_gate_failure_kind`/`_gate_failure_detail`, `resolve_prelock_full_suite_verdict`)
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` (guard baseline / ownership exclusion)
- `skill/implement/tests/` (finish-gate and guard regression tests)

## Impact

An agent finishing a work item keeps the suite's real verdict when another session happens to be writing files at the same time, instead of losing ~10 minutes of suite work and a claim to a false red.
