# `audit_runner.py issue <id>` must audit that item only — never drain the host-wide audit queue

## Problem statement

A single-item audit (`audit_runner.py issue <id>`, including the ship release gate's `issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` remediation call) silently continues into a **global, host-wide batch drain** after the primary audit succeeds: when the shared `audit-batch` priority queue holds ≥ 2 entries — which may all belong to *other* projects — the same process audits up to 5 foreign work items within the same 30-minute window. This inflates a one-item audit to tens of minutes (48 min observed), consumes the release gate's remediation budget, and has been observed surfacing another project's acceptance criteria and variance rows inside a SorraAgents item's persisted Phase-2 report — a contamination path that could produce a false "Ready to close: Yes" at the release gate.

## Users

- **Release engineer / ship skill operator**: runs `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` as a bounded gate remediation and needs it to finish within the 29-minute per-item budget, auditing exactly the item under gate.
- **Agent implementing a work item**: runs the audit skill on its own item and expects the verdict to describe *that* item's evidence only.
- **Downtime/audit dispatcher (herdr)**: needs a single, explicit entry point that drains the machine-wide queue across projects.

Example user stories:

- As a release engineer, when the gate re-audits item X, the run takes as long as auditing X takes and never audits items from another repository, so the remediation budget is spent on the blocker.
- As an implementing agent, I can trust that a "Yes" verdict persisted on my item was derived from my item's acceptance criteria and repository evidence, not another project's.
- As the audit dispatcher, I can still ask for one drain window across all projects by running `audit_runner.py batch` explicitly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `audit_runner.py issue <id>` audits **only** `<id>` (and, unchanged, its children): with two or more foreign entries queued in the `audit-batch` queue, a single-item run audits none of them, leaves every entry queued, and its exit code and persisted verdict are unaffected by their presence.
- The post-audit drain is **explicit** for `issue`: it runs only when the operator passes `--batch-drain`; neither the default invocation nor `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` (which no longer switches the drain on) can trigger it, while `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` still disables an explicitly requested drain.
- An explicitly requested `issue --batch-drain` drains only entries whose stamped owning project root matches the audited item's owning root; entries owned by other projects, and legacy entries with no stamped root, remain queued untouched and are reported as skipped in the batch metrics line.
- `audit_runner.py batch` remains the single explicit cross-project drain entry point: its priming, per-item worklog routing (each item audited against its own project's `.worklog`), priority/FIFO order, and wall-clock budget are unchanged.
- A regression test proves report isolation: a run started for a SorraAgents item that sees a foreign queued entry produces no persisted audit and no `wl` write for the foreign entry, and a persisted report's acceptance-criteria and variance rows derive only from the audited item's (and its children's) own worklog data.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (batch-drain paragraph), `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (batch-drain activation/queueing/configuration sections), the `--batch-drain`/`--no-batch-drain` help text and the `cmd_issue` docstring are updated to state that `issue` is single-item by default and `batch` is the cross-project drain.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A single-item audit now finishes auditing that item and stops, so a release-gate remediation or an agent's own audit can no longer be hijacked by another project's queued work and can no longer report another project's evidence under this item's name.

## Constraints

- Keep the `batch` subcommand's cross-project dispatch intact (LP-0MW96A9GW009KVF7 AC3): do **not** partition the queue by project or rename the queue — a dispatcher must still be able to drain all projects in one explicit window.
- Skipped entries must never be dropped: foreign and legacy entries stay in the queue for their own project's drain, and repeated runs must leave the queue byte-for-byte equivalent (idempotent).
- Children of the audited item remain in scope exactly as today (child audits, `--audit-children` cascade, in-main-slot child screens are unaffected).
- Any `skill/shared/queue.py` change must be additive and backward compatible — the queue is used by other skills and by tests.
- Release gate bounds must be respected: `SHIP_AUDIT_REMEDIATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (29 min per item) must no longer be consumed by foreign work.
- Behaviour change is documented loudly because operators may currently rely on the implicit drain (the documented migration path is `audit_runner.py batch`).

## Existing state

- `cmd_issue` ends with `if rc == 0 and batch_drain is not False: if _batch_drain_enabled(): _maybe_run_batch_drain(ctx)` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~18681). `batch_drain=None` (the CLI default) therefore resolves to ON, and `_batch_drain_enabled()` returns True unless `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` (~5722).
- `_maybe_run_batch_drain` gates on the **global** queue depth (`PriorityQueue("audit-batch")`, `_batch_drain_should_run(len(queue))`, ≥ 2 entries) with no project scoping (~18690).
- `_batch_drain_cycle` dequeues strictly by priority/timestamp, skips only `audit:` tickets, the caller's own id and duplicates; the entry's `project_root` is passed to the audit callback for worklog routing, but foreign entries are audited regardless (~5839).
- `_batch_audit_one` re-runs the full `cmd_issue` pipeline for each drained item against `<project_root>/.worklog` and with `batch_drain=False` (~18712).
- The queue is host-wide (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/audit-batch`) and shared by every project on the machine (`skill/shared/queue.py::PriorityQueue`).
- The ship skill's gate remediation calls `audit_runner.py issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`, `check-final-validation.js`, `refresh-audits.js`) with no `--no-batch-drain`, so a gate run inherits the global drain.
- Observed evidence (from the item report): repeated `Warning: audit launched from /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents but work item RISE-… is owned by /home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising` lines inside an SA-item run, `Audit slot acquired: … ticket=audit:RISE-…` in the same run, and one single-item audit lasting 48 minutes (10:58 → 11:46).
- The `--batch-drain` / `--no-batch-drain` CLI flags exist but the default (auto) path is what fires; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` is documented as an opt-out, not an opt-in (~19288).

## Desired change

1. Resolve the `issue` drain default to **off**: `batch_drain=None` means "do not drain"; only an explicit `--batch-drain` opts in for that run. Keep `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` as a hard disable of any requested drain and drop its "auto-on" meaning (document the change).
2. Scope any explicit `issue`-run drain to the audited item's owning project root: entries whose stamped `project_root` differs — and legacy entries with no stamped root — are left in the queue and counted in the metrics line (e.g. `skipped_foreign=N`, `skipped_unattributed=M`). Implement via an additive filtered-next helper in `skill/shared/queue.py` (or an internal peek/remove loop that never drops an entry).
3. Keep `cmd_batch` (the `batch` subcommand) unchanged as the explicit cross-project drain, and keep `_batch_audit_one`'s per-item worklog routing.
4. Add regression tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py`: (a) `cmd_issue` does not invoke `_maybe_run_batch_drain` with the default invocation; (b) a `--batch-drain` run with mixed SA-/foreign queue entries audits only the SA- ones and leaves the foreign entries queued; (c) legacy rootless entries are skipped, not audited; (d) an `Audit batch drain:` line reports the skips. Add a report-isolation test (see AC5) in the same suite or the adjacent `cmd_issue` trigger tests.
5. Update documentation: `skill/audit/SKILL.md` batch-drain paragraph, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (activation trigger, queueing model, configuration table, CLI notes), the `cmd_issue`/`_maybe_run_batch_drain` docstrings, CLI help text, and any ship-reference sentence that implies a gate `issue` call may drain.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue` drain trigger (~18681), `_maybe_run_batch_drain` (~18690), `_batch_drain_cycle` (~5839), `_batch_audit_one` (~18712), `_batch_drain_enabled` (~5722), CLI flags (~19288), batch-drain constants/docstrings (~345–390).
- `skill/shared/queue.py` — additive project-filtered dequeue helper on `PriorityQueue` (or a "next matching entry" method); must not lose skipped entries.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` — trigger/scoping/skip-metric/legacy-entry regression tests; `_fake_context`, `_enqueue_with_root`, `_recording_audit_one` helpers already exist.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — command-level test that a single-item run with foreign queue entries never calls `cmd_issue` for them (existing cmd_issue trigger/mocking harness).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — line ~405 batch-drain paragraph.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — batch drain section (~729–790) and CLI/config tables.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — release-gate remediation contract (note that `issue` is now strictly single-item).
- `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md` — deployment boundary sentence referencing batch drain (check for stale claims).

## Related work

- `SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5` — added batch-drain mode (the automatic post-audit drain this item removes from `issue`).
- `LP-0MW96A9GW009KVF7` (parent `LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS`) — host-wide queue with per-entry owning project root and per-item worklog routing; this item keeps that routing and its explicit `batch` drain.
- `SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM` — audit admission priority queue (separate queue, unchanged).
- `SA-0MRL8W6V7006LH5I` — child not ready ⇒ parent not ready (the child-scope rule this item leaves untouched).
- `SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL` — bound host-wide audit fan-out and detect orphans (host-wide concurrency context).
- `SA-0MVQ6P2P2008SDPV`, `SA-0MVQ6P06Z007MMMG`, `SA-0MVQ6OXOA003RQFU`, `SA-0MVKXNWRS005EKBM` — single-item audit wall-clock reduction work: the unexplained 48-minute single-item run is exactly the variance these measurements chased.
- `SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15` — per-audit `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` (cross-repo routing foundation that makes the observed foreign warnings possible).
- `SA-0MWQZGQVH003JWG1` — open: audit code-quality scan resolves `--code-root` file scope against the launch cwd (another cross-repo scoping defect).
- `SA-0MWROFAG800719G4` — open: driven child in a foreign-project worktree cannot resolve its owning worklog store (cross-project routing family).
- `SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B` — `discovered-from` (release-review parent).
- `SA-0MW92TODX00064XQ` — ship-triggered marker; the gate path that must stay strictly single-item.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Contamination mechanism not root-caused.** The observed cross-project AC/variance text in an SA-item report has no confirmed code path; the structural fix (never audit a foreign item inside an `issue` run) removes the observed vector. Mitigation: AC5 requires a report-isolation regression test, and the implementation must state (in the work item) the mechanism it proved or the residual risk if it cannot reproduce it.
- **Dispatcher reliance.** If the herdr/downtime dispatcher currently relies on `issue` auto-drain, it must switch to `audit_runner.py batch` (explicit). Assumption (documented, not gating): the dispatcher uses `batch` or pre-enqueues, per `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, both of which present `batch` as the production drain entry point.
- **Behaviour-change surprise.** Operators who relied on the implicit drain will see queued items stop progressing after `issue` runs. Mitigation: loud documentation update plus a stderr note when foreign entries are present but not drained.
- **Queue helper scope creep.** A full per-project queue partition would regress the intentional cross-project dispatcher behaviour; not in scope. Keep the change additive and minimal in `skill/shared/queue.py`.
- **Scope-creep risk (recorded, not implemented):** investigating unrelated cross-project routing defects (`SA-0MWQZGQVH003JWG1`, `SA-0MWROFAG800719G4`) is separate work; they are linked, not absorbed.

## Plan (decomposition)

Planned by the plan skill on 2026-11-26. Five vertical-slice children; TDD is applied inside each feature child and two children are standalone verification slices.

| # | Work item | Type | Covers | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Make issue audit single-item by default (SA-0MWY4MA1G0079P5S) | feature | AC1, AC2 | — |
| 2 | Scope issue batch drain to owning project (SA-0MWY4MDMY004DPMT) | feature | AC3 | 1 |
| 3 | Prove report isolation for a single-item audit (SA-0MWY4M2RE002UM2A) | task (verification) | AC5 | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Update batch-drain documentation and help text (SA-0MWY4MHQH00582Q0) | docs | AC6, AC7 | 1, 2 |
| 5 | Verify batch drain and full suite unchanged (SA-0MWY4M6EM000GCE9) | task (verification) | AC4, AC8 | 1, 2, 3, 4 |

**Execution order:** 1 -> 2 -> (3, 4) -> 5. Between phases, re-read the next item's description and update it if the preceding phase changed the design (e.g. if the root comparison needs `_same_git_repository`, record it on item 2 before item 3 starts).

**Vertical-slice phasing:** every child cuts through all layers it needs end-to-end (code + tests, or docs + help text, or verification + evidence). There is no "all code, then all tests" horizontal phase. TDD is applied within each feature child (failing test first, then implementation); a standalone red test item would leave the tree red and fail the implement skill's changed-scope gate, so the tree-level test-first slices are item 3 (report isolation) and item 5 (batch non-regression + full suite), which gate or follow the implementation they verify.

**Assumption gate:** item 2 records a resolved assumption for an undeterminable audited-item owning root (drain nothing, report the skips). No new producer decisions were required.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-26: Plan complete. Created 5 children (2 feature vertical slices, 2 verification tasks, 1 docs item) and wired AC1/AC2 -> item 1, AC3 -> item 2, AC5 -> item 3, AC6/AC7 -> item 4, AC4/AC8 -> item 5. Dependencies: 2<-1; 3<-1,2; 4<-1,2; 5<-1,2,3,4.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should `issue <id>` keep *any* automatic drain, or must a drain always be explicit?" — Answer (item report, Expected section): "An `issue <id>` invocation audits **that item only** (its children excepted); draining the cross-project queue must be an explicit batch/dispatcher action, or strictly scoped to the invoking project." Source: `SA-0MWWE4OI1006OC42` description. Interpretation recorded: make the drain explicit (`--batch-drain`) *and* project-scope it, since both halves of the sentence can be satisfied together.
- Q: "Which path does the release gate use, and does it opt out of the drain?" — Answer (repo research): `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (~953), `check-final-validation.js` (~480) and `refresh-audits.js` (~132) each spawn `python3 <runner> issue <id> --strict --ship-triggered` with no `--no-batch-drain`, so the gate inherits the auto-drain. Source: `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` (remediation budget: 29 min/item, 30 min total).
- Q: "Is the batch queue host-wide or per project?" — Answer (repo research): host-wide — `PriorityQueue` stores entries under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-semaphores/<name>`, and `AUDIT_BATCH_QUEUE_NAME = "audit-batch"` is a single name for every project; entries carry an owning `project_root` so a drain can *route* them, but nothing prevents a drain from *taking* them. Sources: `skill/shared/queue.py::_default_lock_dir`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~349, ~5803–5860, ~5839).
- Q: "Is there already an opt-out?" — Answer (repo research): yes, `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` or `--no-batch-drain`, but both are opt-outs; the default (`batch_drain=None`) resolves to ON, which is the defect. Source: `audit_runner.py::_batch_drain_enabled` (~5722), CLI flags (~19288).
- Q: "Does anything depend on the implicit drain?" — Answer (repo research): no code path in this repo does; docs present `audit_runner.py batch` as the production drain entry point (`skill/audit/SKILL.md` ~405, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` ~731–790). The external herdr dispatcher is out of repo; assumption recorded under Risks.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** – Add batch drain mode to audit runner (completed)
- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** – Evaluate whether idle-gate relaxation for audit dispatch is needed (completed)
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** – Integrate audit runner with bounded priority queue (replaces fail-fast) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0msrlecw2001aa15, 0mtg5ryh8005rqnm, 0mtg5tp5z008qbl5, 0muiumo7t00639fl, 0mw7z77ki005mk0b (+426 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msrlecw2001aa15, 0mtg5ryh8005rqnm, 0mtg5tp5z008qbl5, 0mw0kzujp0019sls, 0mw7z77ki005mk0b (+410 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: able, absorbed, ac3, ac5, acceptance (+405 more)

### Plan-session questions & assumptions (2026-11-26)

- Q: "When an explicit `issue --batch-drain` cannot determine the audited item's owning project root, should it drain nothing or fall back to an unfiltered drain?" — Assumption (agent research, safety-preserving default): drain nothing and report every entry as skipped. No entry can be proven to belong to the item, and an unfiltered drain is precisely the defect being fixed. Recorded on item 2 (`SA-0MWY4MDMY004DPMT`). Not a producer handoff: the answer follows directly from Desired change 2.
- Q: "How should owning roots be compared — literal resolved path or git-common-dir?" — Assumption (agent research): compare resolved path strings first; if worktree/symlink divergence surfaces in tests, reuse the existing `_same_git_repository` helper (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). Recorded as a risky assumption on item 2.
- Q: "Does test-first ordering require separate red test items?" — Decision (agent, per repository precedent): implement each feature as a vertical slice with TDD inside it, plus standalone verification slices (items 3 and 5). A standalone red test item would leave the tree red between sessions and fail the implement skill's changed-scope test gate.

# In-main-slot child verdicts cannot be persisted by a session

## Problem statement

The documented in-main-slot resume cycle — "perform each emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen, persist the child audit, then re-run the parent to collect the verdicts" — cannot be completed when the session persists the child verdict with `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>`. The parent re-run both **rejects** the text verdict (it is not accepted by the reuse path) and **clobbers** it by persisting a fresh `partial — main-session review` placeholder over it. A session that follows the documented contract therefore livelocks: only a lucky single run (parent screen + child screen in the same invocation) can pass.

## Users

- **Producer/Agent running a parent audit**: services the emitted child screens and expects the persisted verdicts to stick and be collected on the next parent run.
- **Herdr/downtime workers**: automate the audit loop; a livelock burns LLM slots and never converges.
- **Release reviewer (ship gate)**: blocks the release because the parent audit can never report `Ready to close: Yes` while a serviced child is re-screened and reset to pending.

Example user stories:

- As an agent servicing an in-main-slot child screen, I want the verdict I persist (via the documented command) to be reused by the parent with zero child `pi` calls, so that the parent converges after one servicing pass.
- As a release reviewer, I want a re-run of the parent audit to honour an already-serviced, fresh child audit instead of overwriting it with a pending placeholder.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Session-persisted verdicts are reused.** After a session services an emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen and persists the child verdict with the documented command (including a `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>` text report carrying a `Ready to close: Yes` line and a per-AC table), a subsequent parent audit collects that child with **zero** child-screening `pi` calls, records the `reused_from` / `child_audit_ready` markers, and emits no `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen for it. This holds for a **gap-mapped** child (parent has gaps and the child owns the gap files) as well as for a child collected by the Phase 1 child-verdict pre-pass.
- **AC2 — A serviced child audit is never clobbered.** A parent re-run must never persist a pending (`partial` + `main-session review`) child report over a stored child audit that is fresh and carries a real, non-pending verdict and AC table — whether that audit was persisted by the runner or by a session via `wl audit-set --audit-file`. The serviced report (verdict + AC table) survives the parent run.
- **AC3 — Documented persist path is exact.** The audit skill and reference document the exact command a session must use to persist a serviced in-main-slot child screen so that reuse accepts it, and the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` payload / `Child screens pending` instruction points to that command. Following **only** the documented steps converges the cycle (no re-emitted screens, no `unserviced_in_main_slot` classification for serviced children).
- **AC4 — Convergence end to end.** After servicing all emitted screens and re-running the parent, the `Child screens pending` gate clears, `pending_child_screens` is empty, the `<id>.pending-screens.json` signal is removed, and the parent report names only genuine remaining parent AC gaps.
- **AC5 — Regression tests.** Unit tests cover: (a) a session-persisted, fingerprint-less `wl audit-set` report (`Ready to close: Yes` + AC table) is reused by the gap-mapped path with zero child screens; (b) the persist-overwrite guard skips a pending child report over such a serviced audit; (c) the documented persist command produces a report the reuse path accepts. No real `pi` or `audit_runner` subprocess is invoked.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant resume-cycle references.
- **AC7 — Full project test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A session can now service an in-main-slot child screen once — persisting the verdict makes it stick, and the next parent run collects it instead of re-screening and clobbering it — so parent audits on epics with gap-mapped children converge instead of livelocking.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken the strict v2 content-freshness gate** for runner-persisted child audits; the new acceptance of session-persisted reports is additive (a fallback), not a relaxation of the fingerprint contract for reports that carry one.
- **`--force` still bypasses reuse** — every child is re-audited under `--force`; the new path must not change that.
- **Lifecycle neutrality is preserved** — a parent-persisted child audit must still never change the child's lifecycle (the existing `_restore_child_pre_audit_lifecycle` contract).
- **No new `wl` schema or CLI field** unless an existing documented option (e.g. `wl audit-set --fingerprint`) is used; any helper must live in the audit runner/skill.
- **The separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`) is unchanged.**
- **Scope-creep risk**: general audit-report parsing improvements, cross-repo consumer ACs (e.g. `LP-0MVOBJGB4001TQ8X`), and unrelated freshness-gate work are out of scope and must be recorded as linked work items rather than folded in.

## Existing state

The residual defect is confined to the paths that require a **v2 content fingerprint**, which a session-written `wl audit-set` report never carries:

- **Gap-mapped re-screen** — `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_phase_children`, parent-first gap-mapped branch (~line 16661): it calls `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict` (~line 9757), which returns `(None, None)` for a fingerprint-less report by design. The child is added to `pending_children` and its `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screen is re-emitted.
- **Persist-overwrite guard** — same function, child-persist loop (~line 16809): it skips persisting only when `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict(...)[0] is not None`, i.e. only for a v2 content-fresh audit. A session-persisted report is not content-fresh, so the pending placeholder is persisted over it (the clobber).
- **Underspecified persist step** — the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` payload (`_emit_in_main_slot_work`, ~line 6513; prompt built in `_phase1_review_child_acs`, ~line 10106) is a READ-ONLY screen prompt and never names a persist command. The `Child screens pending` gate (`_assemble_child_audit_report`, ~line 8597) and the pending-screens signal instructions (`_write_pending_screens_signal`, ~line 8118) say only "persist the child audit". The session reasonably chooses `wl audit-set --audit-file <report>`, which stores the text but no v2 fingerprint line.
- **Why the Phase 1 pre-pass is not the blocker** — the non-gap Phase 1 pre-pass (~line 16095) uses `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~line 9623), which does accept fingerprint-less reports through the legacy time-gate floor when `auditedAt` is fresh. The reproduction hit the gap-mapped branch, which is strictly content-fingerprint-gated. The clobber, however, can poison the time gate on later runs by bumping the child's `updatedAt`.

Reproduction evidence (v0.2.0 release review, 2026-11-25, parent `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK`): three children (`SA-0MWFFXNNM00148IX`, `SA-0MWFFXKKA005CLVK`, `SA-0MWFFXQNT002LB8T`) were serviced and persisted with `wl audit-set --audit-file`; all showed `readyToClose=true`; the next parent run re-emitted the screens, overwrote the verdicts with `partial — main-session review`, and classified all three `[unserviced_in_main_slot]`.

## Desired change

Make the documented resume cycle work end to end for a session-persisted child audit, without weakening the v2 gate for runner-persisted audits. Any of the item's originally proposed directions is acceptable; the preferred combination is:

1. **Accept a session-persisted verdict on the reuse path (fallback).** When no v2 fingerprint is present, fall back to the legacy time-gated verdict acceptance (`_get_child_audit_verdict` semantics) for the gap-mapped branch, so a fresh `wl audit-set` report with a parseable `Ready to close:` line and AC table is collected with zero child `pi` calls. Use the same fallback in the checkpoint-resume re-resolution if it is reachable there.
2. **Guard the persist overwrite.** Broaden the persist-overwrite guard so a pending child report is never persisted over **any** fresh stored child audit carrying a real non-pending verdict, not only a v2 content-fresh one. Keep `--force` and the runner-persisted reuse markers authoritative.
3. **Document the exact persist command.** Either document the existing `wl audit-set` invocation (and, if it is sufficient, the `--fingerprint` value the session must pass) or add a small runner helper that assembles/persists the report with the v2 fingerprint line. Embed the exact command in the emitted screen payload and the pending-screens instruction so following the docs alone converges.
4. **Regression-test the three behaviours** in AC5 with fixtures that model a session-written fingerprint-less report (no real subprocess).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_phase_children` gap-mapped branch (~16661) and child-persist guard (~16809); `_get_child_content_fresh_verdict` (~9757); `_get_child_audit_verdict` (~9623); `_child_acs_from_own_audit` (~9860); `_emit_in_main_slot_work` (~6513); `_phase1_review_child_acs` (~10106); `_write_pending_screens_signal` (~8118); `_assemble_child_audit_report` gate (~8597).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — in-main-slot resume-cycle section (~227–241).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — resume-cycle composition (~1293–1305) and child-verdict reuse (~1418).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — end-to-end resume tests (`TestResumeCycleEndToEnd`).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_freshness.py` — freshness / reuse tests.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_persist_demotion.py` — persist guard tests.

## Related work

- `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK` — source item (discovered-from); its 2026-11-25 comment records the full clobber sequence.
- `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I` — partial-overlap predecessor: gap-mapped reuse + persist-overwrite guard, scoped to **content-fresh (v2)** audits only; it deliberately leaves fingerprint-less audits re-screened. This item is the residual gap.
- `SA-0MSQJA0WL006UJ3T` — child verdict reuse (LP-0MSQ32MF200675AR) foundation.
- `SA-0MSQJABHZ0018APE` — content-gate child verdict reuse in parent audits.
- `SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S` / `SA-0MW2J7O3D0044SFM` — in-main-slot resume + checkpoint re-resolution (the resume cycle this bug breaks).
- `SA-0MVAWFUU0004VW45` / `SA-0MVAWFYZE0040SQ3` — unserviced in-main-slot assessment and reason diagnostics (reporting side; this item is the persistence side).
- `SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN` — content-freshness contract docs.
- `SA-0MVAWFPVU001E1T0` — unserviced in-main-slot verdict tests.
- `SA-0MWIXJ84T000GBWG` — fingerprint_kind/age reporting when a cached verdict is reused (related, blocked).

Potentially related docs:

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (resume-cycle composition, freshness gate, child-verdict reuse).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (in-main-slot mode, child-audit execution contract).
- `docs/dev/audit-reliability-rca.md`, `docs/dev/audit-child-demotion-rca.md` (prior cliff/loop analyses).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Which of the three proposed remediation directions (a: accept `wl audit-set` text verdicts; b: provide a documented persist command; c: honour an already-fresh stored child audit on re-run) should be implemented?**
  - **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** Implement the preferred combination in *Desired change* — (a)+(c) in the runner plus (b) in the documentation/emitted instruction. Rationale: the source item explicitly accepts any of the three; this combination removes the livelock end to end and keeps the v2 gate intact for runner-persisted audits. Evidence: source description ("Expected: Either (a) … or (b) … or (c)") and the 2026-11-25 comment on `SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK`. This is a design assumption, not an open producer question; the plan/implement stages may refine the mechanism.
- **Q: Does `wl audit-set` guarantee `updatedAt == auditedAt`, so the legacy time-gate fallback can accept a fingerprint-less session report?**
  - **Answer (research):** The audit docs state that the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes` path sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` (`skill/audit/SKILL.md` line 49; `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`). Implementation must verify this holds for `--audit-file` too and, if not, either use the report's own audited timestamp or add a fingerprint to the persisted report. Source: repo docs.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I`?**
  - **Answer (research):** No full duplicate. That item's AC1/AC2 are explicitly scoped to content-fresh (v2-fingerprinted) audits and leave fingerprint-less audits re-screened; this item covers the session-persisted `wl audit-set` text-verdict case that the predecessor left open. Recorded as a duplicate-check comment on this item. Source: `SA-0MVZ3SMK6007431I` description + code comments at `audit_runner.py` ~16661/16809.
- **Q: Is the clobber also reachable via the non-gap Phase 1 pre-pass?**
  - **Answer (research):** The non-gap pre-pass uses `_get_child_audit_verdict` (time-gate fallback) and so can accept a fresh fingerprint-less report; the reproduction hit the gap-mapped branch, which is strictly content-fingerprint-gated. The clobber guard is shared, so the fix must cover both branches for consistency. Source: `audit_runner.py` ~16095, ~16661, ~16809.
data.title: In-main-slot child verdicts cannot be persisted by a session: reuse rejects `wl audit-set` text verdicts and a parent re-run clobbers serviced verdicts

data.description:
# A failed dev→main sync aborts the verified post-release tail: the release ships but every item stays open and no notification is sent

## Problem statement

`run-release.js` runs the post-release tail in an order where the network-dependent
`syncDevWithMain()` (Step 7) executes **before** merge verification (Step 8), the Discord
notification (Step 8.5) and work-item closure (Step 9). A transport-only failure on that
single `git push origin dev` therefore returns `finish(5)` and silently discards the whole
verified tail — the release has already landed on `main`, yet no notification is sent and all
shipped items stay `completed/in_review`. There is also no supported way to finish a
partially-applied release: re-running `run-release.js` trips the newly-created-tag gate
(exit 14) by design.

## Users

- **Release manager (operator)** — runs `/skill:ship release` and needs a release that
  landed to be fully recorded, even when one later network call fails.
- **Autonomous release agent / driven session** — must not be left with a half-applied
  release it cannot legally finish with any supported command.
- **Producer** — relies on the Discord announcement and on shipped items reaching
  `completed/done` without manual `node -e` scripting.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when `git push origin dev` fails with "Connection to github.com
  closed by remote host", the release still verifies, announces and closes its items, and I
  am told exactly which single command re-syncs `dev`.
- As a release manager recovering a half-applied release (v0.2.0 on 2026-11-26), I run
  `node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --finish-release 0.2.0` and the tail
  completes idempotently without a new tag, merge or PR.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Tail reordered so network-dependent work cannot suppress verified work.** The
   post-release order becomes: verify release merge (gating) → Discord notification →
   close work items → branch cleanup → sync dev with main **last**. Existing gates are
   preserved unchanged: a failed `verifyReleaseMerge` still exits 11 before any
   notification or close, and the newly-created-tag gate still exits 14 before any
   post-release step.
2. **A dev-sync failure is non-fatal.** When `syncDevWithMain()` fails after the tail has
   run, the run completes with exit code 0 (the release *did* land), prints a loud
   `⚠️` warning naming the failure and the exact recovery command (`git push origin dev`),
   and reports the sync outcome in the timing/summary output. Exit code 5 is no longer
   emitted by a full release run (documented as reserved).
3. **Dev sync retries transient transport errors.** `syncDevWithMain()` retries only
   transport-class failures (connection reset/closed by remote host, TLS/proxy errors,
   timeouts) — default 3 attempts with exponential backoff — and does not retry
   deterministic failures (merge conflict, non-fast-forward rejection, missing ref).
   Attempts/backoff are injectable so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real
   repository.
4. **`--finish-release <version>` completes a partially-applied tail idempotently.** The new
   entry point runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync —
   with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump, no Code Freeze marker, and
   without tripping the newly-created-tag gate (provenance comes from
   `verifyReleaseMerge` instead). It exits 0 on success, 11 when merge verification fails,
   13 on an invalid/unknown argument, and nothing is executed on argument error.
5. **Notification provenance is explicit on the recovery path.** `sendReleaseNotification`
   keeps failing closed by default (a pre-existing tag is never announced); the
   `--finish-release` path supplies the verified-release provenance explicitly so a
   confirmed release is announced exactly once, and re-running it does not double-notify
   (or the duplicate is documented and accepted).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests cover: tail ordering (verify/notify/close before dev sync, and
   dev-sync failure not aborting them), transport-only retry policy (retries then
   succeeds; deterministic failure not retried), the `--finish-release` entry point
   (gate bypass, exit codes, no merge/PR/tag calls, argument-error inertness) and
   idempotent re-run. Existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` and
   `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stay green.
7. **Documentation.** `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (post-release step order, exit-code table,
   partial-release recovery section) and `docs/dev/release-process.md` (recovery runbook)
   describe the new order, the non-fatal dev sync and the `--finish-release` command.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A release that already landed can no longer be left half-applied: a transient network
reset on the final `dev` push no longer costs the announcement and the closure of every
shipped item, and an operator has one documented command that finishes the tail instead of
hand-rolled `node -e` scripts.

## Constraints

- **Purely internal tooling surface.** No work-item data-model, worklog-store or
  notification-format change; `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` reload/close semantics stay as
  they are.
- **Existing safety gates must not weaken.** The newly-created-tag gate (exit 14) and
  `verifyReleaseMerge` (exit 11) stay hard gates for a normal release; `--finish-release`
  may bypass *only* the tag-creation gate, and only because it proves the release by
  origin-tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main` verification instead.
- **No new dependencies**; the retry/backoff must not make unit tests slow (injectable
  clock/sleep).
- **Worktree/main-checkout rule unchanged:** release operations still run from the main
  checkout, never from a worktree.

## Evidence (original report)

- `/tmp/ship-release7.log`: `⚠️  Failed to sync dev with main: … Connection to github.com
  closed by remote host.`; the timing table shows `Step 7: sync dev with main 0.000` and no
  Steps 8-10.
- PR #730 merged, tag `v0.2.0` created, `origin/main` = `ad34d578cd` — the release landed,
  yet items stayed `completed/in_review` (e.g. SA-0MWFFX49M0016KOK, SA-0MWFP1E9P0027EOE) and
  were closed manually by importing `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` in a one-off node script.
- Re-running `run-release.js` was impossible: `v0.2.0` already existed, so the
  newly-created-tag gate would exit 14 by design.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` (2134 lines): Step 7 `syncDevWithMain()` at ~line
  2013 returning `finish(5)`; Step 8 verify/tag gate at ~2056; Step 8.5 notification at
  ~2084; Step 9 close at ~2092; Step 10 cleanup after. Arg parsing via `BOOLEAN_FLAGS` /
  `VALUE_FLAGS` / `parseReleaseArgs()` (exit 13 on unknown flag) at ~line 145-250; a
  pre-flight-only early-exit precedent (`--refresh-audits` → `runRefreshAuditsAction`)
  at ~line 1743.
- `syncDevWithMain(options)` already takes an injectable `options.run` command runner
  (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) — the retry loop can reuse that seam.
- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` is already idempotent (`Shipped in v<version>` marker,
  version-exact, SA-0MUECDK14002J37J) and verifies persisted closure.
- `sendReleaseNotification()` already fails closed on provenance (`preRunTags`).
- No `--finish-release` / resume path exists anywhere (verified by repo grep).

## Desired change

1. Move the `syncDevWithMain()` call after verify → notify → close → cleanup; make its
   failure a warning that does not change the exit code.
2. Wrap the sync's command runner in a bounded retry for transport-class errors.
3. Add `--finish-release <version>`: parse it as a value flag, route it to a new
   `runFinishReleaseAction(flags)` **before** `setCodeFreezeMarker`/`runReleaseImpl`
   (mirroring `--refresh-audits`), and have it run the tail with an explicit
   verified-release provenance and no tag gate.
4. Update `WRAPPER_USAGE`, the SKILL.md exit-code table + release-process step list, and
   add a partial-release recovery section to `docs/dev/release-process.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — reorder the tail (~2007-2115); add the retry loop
  to `syncDevWithMain` (~1495); add `--finish-release` to `VALUE_FLAGS`, `parseReleaseArgs`,
  `WRAPPER_USAGE` (~145-250); add `runFinishReleaseAction` and its call site next to the
  `--refresh-audits` pre-flight (~1743); add the non-fatal dev-sync warning.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — add/confirm an explicit provenance option so a
  verified `--finish-release` can announce without a pre-run tag snapshot.
- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` — retry-policy and ordering coverage
  (injected runner/sleep).
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-finish-release.mjs` *(new)* — entry-point behaviour, exit
  codes, no merge/PR/tag side effects, idempotent re-run, argument-error inertness.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` *(new)* — verified tail ordering and
  dev-sync failure not suppressing notify/close.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — exit-code table (5 reserved), release-process step order,
  recovery section for `--finish-release`.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — partially-applied release recovery runbook.

## Related work

- **SA-0MQAUIMBT009351X** — Post-release dev sync: return to dev and merge main after ship
  (completed): introduced `syncDevWithMain()`, the step this item re-orders and retries.
- **SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA** — Gate post-release steps on a newly created tag (completed):
  source of the exit-14 gate that makes a re-run of a partially-applied release impossible
  today; this item adds the supported recovery path *around* that gate.
- **SA-0MUECDK14002J37J** — Run-release close idempotency (`Shipped in v<version>` marker,
  completed): makes re-running the close step safe, a precondition for `--finish-release`.
- **SA-0MV0QEI3Q0063KH3** — Discord announcement provenance guard (completed): the fail-closed
  notifier behaviour the recovery path must supply provenance for.
- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** — Test infra: concurrent full-suite runs deadlock (completed):
  gave `syncDevWithMain`/`verifyReleaseMerge` the injectable command-runner seam reused here.
- **SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT** — Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically
  (open): same non-blocking-tail area; independent failure mode, no overlap in fix.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — the documentation surface
  describing the tail order and exit codes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Should a dev-sync failure keep a non-zero exit code (today's `5`)? **Recommended:**
  exit 0 with a warning — a landed release is a success, and a non-zero code would let
  automation misreport the release as failed. — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):**
  exit 0 with a `⚠️` warning naming `git push origin dev`; exit 5 documented as reserved.
  Source: work item "Expected" item 1 ("must not be fatal to the release result");
  research: existing codes 2/4/5/6/7/9/10/11/12/13/14 in `skill/ship/SKILL.md`.
- **Q:** How many retry attempts and which errors are retryable? **Recommended:** 3 attempts,
  exponential backoff, transport-class errors only. — **Answer (agent, documented
  assumption):** as recommended; backoff/attempts injectable for tests. Source: work item
  item 2; research: `syncDevWithMain` already exposes `options.run`
  (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86).
- **Q:** Should `--finish-release` bypass the newly-created-tag gate? **Recommended:** yes,
  substituting `verifyReleaseMerge` (origin tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main`) as provenance.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** yes; the gate exists to stop *spurious*
  releases, and the recovery path proves the release by the origin/ancestor facts instead.
  Source: work item item 3; `skill/ship/SKILL.md` § Newly-created-tag gate.
- **Q:** Can re-running `--finish-release` double-post the Discord announcement?
  **Recommended:** accept at-most-once semantics from the existing notifier and document
  idempotence for close/cleanup/sync only. — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):**
  recommended; note it in the SKILL.md recovery section because no send-marker exists.
  Research: `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` has no dedupe store.
- **Q:** Is a separate work item needed for idempotent notification (a sent-marker)?
  **Recommended:** no — record as an out-of-scope opportunity. — **Answer (agent):** recorded
  as a scope-creep risk below, not created (single-operator tool, low value today).

### Plan round (2026-11-26)

- **Q:** How should the change be decomposed — (a) 6 children as 3 test/verification items then 3 implementation items, (b) 3 children each carrying its own tests, (c) 1 item for the whole description?
  **Recommended:** (a) — the plan skill requires test/verification items before implementation items, and the three behaviours have independent test files.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" — no objection raised, so the recommendation was adopted: **final (a)**. Source: plan interview round 1, this work item's session `herdr-1795698218-2137099-6223`.
- **Q:** Transport-error classification for the retry — (a) allowlist (retry only recognised transport signatures; anything unrecognised is not retried) vs (b) denylist (retry everything except known-deterministic failures)?
  **Recommended:** (a) — `git merge` is not idempotent, so an unknown failure must fail closed rather than be replayed.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" → **final (a)** allowlist. Recorded in child SA-0MWXMTQ4Q001N0WJ.
- **Q:** Where do the documentation updates land — (a) folded into the implementation children (vertical slices) or (b) one separate docs child depending on both?
  **Recommended:** (a) — the plan skill's vertical-slice rule; a standalone docs item would be a horizontal layer.
  — **Answer (operator):** "continue" → **final (a)**; step order + exit-code reservations go with the reorder child, the recovery runbook + `WRAPPER_USAGE` with the `--finish-release` child.
- **Q:** Test-first children cannot commit failing tests (the changed-scope gate must be green), so how do the red-first halves land?
  **Recommended:** commit the new tests with `node:test`'s `{ todo: true }` — the analogue of the `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` red-first pattern already used in this repository.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** as recommended. Research: `git show a45899877` (child SA-0MW3GCHEL001G8CP) shows the xfail red-first pattern; `node:test` has no xfail, and `{ todo: true }` is the closest fail-safe equivalent (a failing todo test does not fail the run). Each implementation child removes its marker.
- **Q:** Where does the retry classifier live, and does a retry replay the whole command sequence?
  **Recommended:** classifier + inner `attemptSync()` next to `syncDevWithMain()`, with every attempt restarting from a fresh `git fetch origin --prune`.
  — **Answer (agent, documented assumption):** as recommended — a retried merge must never compound stale state; the existing `options.run` seam (SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86) carries the fake runner.
- **Q:** Should the notifier gain a sent-marker so `--finish-release` re-runs never double-announce?
  **Recommended:** no — out of scope (see the existing Appendix entry above), documented as at-most-once.
  — **Answer (agent):** unchanged from the intake Appendix; not re-asked. No child created for a dedupe store.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** touching the notifier could grow into building an announcement
  dedupe/marker store — explicitly out of scope; only the provenance plumbing changes.
- **Gate weakening risk:** a bug in `--finish-release` routing could let a normal release
  skip the exit-14 gate. Mitigation: the flag is only honoured by the recovery action
  before `runReleaseImpl` is entered; the normal path's gate is untouched, and a unit test
  asserts it still fires.
- **Reordering risk:** moving `syncDevWithMain` last changes repository state during the
  close/cleanup steps (still on the release branch, `main` not yet merged into `dev`) —
  mitigated because those steps operate on tags/`origin/main`, not the local checkout.
- **Retry risk:** retrying a non-idempotent `git merge` could compound state. Mitigation:
  retry only transport-class errors, re-running the full command sequence from a fresh
  fetch, and never retry conflicts/rejections.
- **Assumption:** a partially-applied release is detectable by the operator from the run
  output/timing report (no new persisted state file is introduced).
## Plan: decomposition (2026-11-26)

Six children — three red-first test items then three implementation items — all
priority `critical`, mapped to the ACs above. Deps: `2←1`, `4←3,2`, `6←5,2`.

| # | Child | Type | Parent ACs | Depends on |
|---|-------|------|------------|------------|
| 1 | Test: tail order and non-fatal dev sync (SA-0MWXMTERQ005HYQ3) | task | 1, 2, 6 | — |
| 2 | Reorder post-release tail, sync dev last (SA-0MWXMTNIV006TJH5) | bug | 1, 2, 7, 8 | 1 |
| 3 | Test: transport-only dev sync retry (SA-0MWXMTIM7006760U) | task | 3, 6 | — |
| 4 | Retry transport errors in dev sync (SA-0MWXMTQ4Q001N0WJ) | bug | 3 | 3, 2 |
| 5 | Test: finish-release recovery entry point (SA-0MWXMTKYB006IBPK) | task | 4, 5, 6 | 2 |
| 6 | Add --finish-release recovery command (SA-0MWXMTSKH0085UZZ) | feature | 4, 5, 7, 8 | 5, 2 |

Execution order: **1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6** (`wl next` resolves it).

**Design decisions**

- The verified tail is extracted into `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({version, prUrl, projectRoot, dryRun, provenance})` so the normal path and the recovery path share one ordering; `runReleaseImpl` loses its duplicated Steps 8-10.
- Retry classification is an **allowlist** of transport signatures (connection reset / closed by remote host, `RPC failed`, `early EOF`, TLS/proxy, DNS, timeouts) — an unknown error is never replayed because `git merge` is not idempotent.
- Test-first children land their tests with `node:test`'s `{ todo: true }` (the `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` analogue used by SA-0MW3GCHEL001G8CP); the matching implementation child removes the marker.
- Docs ride along with their slice: the reorder child updates the SKILL.md step order and reserves exit code 5; the `--finish-release` child adds the exit-code table entries, recovery section and `docs/dev/release-process.md` runbook.
- Notification dedupe on re-run stays out of scope (documented at-most-once); no sent-marker store is introduced.
- Related, non-overlapping: SA-0MWXIXV2R008MRT3 (wrapper timeout leaves the main checkout on an orphan release branch) — independent failure mode, no shared fix.

**Vertical-slice note:** the three test items are deliberately test-only — they are the red-first halves of three vertical slices, per the plan skill's test-first ordering rule. Every implementation item carries code + tests + docs. Between phases, re-read the next child's description: child 2 lands the shared helper that children 4 and 6 build on.

## Plan: changelog

## Goal

Raise the release-script default timeout and add start-branch bookkeeping plus `ETIMEDOUT` recovery to the ship wrapper, so a timed-out release leaves the main checkout in its original state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The wrapper's default `SHIP_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS` is ≥ 3 600 000 ms (60 min), justified against the observed 1 982 s Step 5 runtime, and remains env-overridable.
- Before spawning the merge script, the wrapper records the checked-out branch and the branch list.
- On `ETIMEDOUT`, the wrapper restores that branch in the main checkout so it is never left on a `release/dev-to-main-*` branch.
- On the same timeout path, the wrapper deletes the orphan `release/dev-to-main-*` branch(es) created by this run — identified by pre/post branch-snapshot diff, not a bare glob. A branch pushed to origin or referenced by an open PR is NOT deleted and is named in the message.
- The timeout error message names exactly what it restored and what it deleted (or refused to delete, with the reason), replacing the current wording; exit code 10 is retained.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` exit-code-10 descriptions are updated to reflect the new default and recovery behaviour.

## Constraints

- Exit code 10 stays the documented timeout contract; no new exit codes.
- Never delete a branch that exists on `origin` or backs an open PR; never `reset --hard` a start branch with local commits.
- Identify orphans by pre/post branch snapshot (no concurrent-run interference).
- The Code Freeze marker's existing `finally` clearing must keep working.
- No behaviour change to `--dry-run`, gating steps or post-release steps.

# Reorder post-release tail, sync dev last

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC1, AC2, AC7, AC8). Makes the
network-dependent `dev` sync the **last** post-release step and its failure
non-fatal, so a verified release can never be suppressed by one transport
error.

## Context

`runReleaseImpl()` currently runs `syncDevWithMain()` as Step 7 and returns
`finish(5)` when it fails, before verify (Step 8), notify (8.5), close (9) and
cleanup (10). Exit code 5 has no other producer in the pipeline. The tail is
also duplicated logic that the sibling `--finish-release` recovery item must
reuse, so extract it as one exported helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The post-release order becomes: verify release merge (gating) → Discord notification → close work items → branch cleanup → sync dev with main last, so network-dependent work cannot suppress verified work.
- Existing gates are preserved unchanged: a failed `verifyReleaseMerge` still exits 11 before any notification or close, and the newly-created-tag gate still exits 14 before any post-release step.
- When `syncDevWithMain()` fails after the tail has run, the run completes with exit code 0 (the release *did* land), prints a loud `⚠️` warning naming the failure and the exact recovery command `git push origin dev`, and reports the sync outcome in the timing/summary output; exit code 5 is no longer emitted by a full release run and is documented as reserved.
- The verified tail is extracted into an exported `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({ version, prUrl, projectRoot, dryRun })` helper reused verbatim by the recovery entry point, with a `sync` outcome in its result object; normal-path ordering, notification, closure and cleanup behaviour are unchanged apart from the sync move.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` documents the new numbered step order, the non-fatal dev sync and exit code 5 as reserved, and existing code comments describing the old order are corrected.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `README.md` entries and any relevant docs-site or wiki references to the old tail order.
- The sibling ordering harness `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` loses its `todo` markers and passes, and the existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` and `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stay green.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- In `runReleaseImpl()`, delete the Step 7 block (~2007-2016) and run the sync **after** the Step 10 cleanup, inside the `if (version)` block, keeping the `stepTimers` entries and appending the sync row to the timing report.
- Wrap the call so a failure only logs `⚠️ Failed to sync dev with main: … Recover with: git push origin dev` and never changes the exit code.
- Extract Steps 8-10 plus the trailing sync into `export function runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` returning `{ version, notified, close, cleanup, sync }`; `runReleaseImpl` calls it and the sibling recovery item calls it too.
- Update `skill/ship/SKILL.md`'s numbered release-step list (steps 9-12 renumber to the new order) and its exit-code table (5 → reserved).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — tail reorder (~2007-2115), new `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` helper
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — release-process step order, exit-code table, dev-sync description
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — only the step-order references touched here; the recovery runbook belongs to the `--finish-release` item
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-tail-order.mjs` — remove `todo` markers

## Impact

A transient network reset on the final `dev` push no longer costs the release its announcement and the closure of every shipped item.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the ordering harness (this item's tests must exist first).

# Retry transport errors in dev sync

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC3). Makes `syncDevWithMain()` retry
transport-class failures with exponential backoff, and only those.

## Context

The 2026-11-26 release died on `Connection to github.com closed by remote host`
— a transient transport fault that a retry would have absorbed. A `git merge`
is not idempotent, so classification must fail closed: an unrecognised error is
never replayed. Classification is therefore an **allowlist** of transport
signatures (documented assumption recorded in the parent Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dev sync retries transient transport errors: `syncDevWithMain()` retries only transport-class failures (connection reset/closed by remote host, `RPC failed`, `early EOF`, TLS/proxy errors, DNS resolution failures, timeouts) — default 3 attempts with exponential backoff — and does not retry deterministic failures (merge conflict, non-fast-forward rejection, missing ref). Attempts/backoff are injectable so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real repository; classification is a strict allowlist, so an unrecognised error is never replayed.
- Default is 3 attempts with exponential backoff, and attempts/backoff/sleep are injectable (`options.attempts`, `options.backoffMs`, `options.sleep`) so unit tests run without sleeping or touching a real repository.
- Deterministic failures are never retried: merge conflict, non-fast-forward `[rejected]` push and missing ref each abort on the first attempt.
- Every retry restarts the full command sequence from a fresh `git fetch origin --prune`, and the exported `run()` default stays `execSync` with git output streamed to stderr.
- The returned `{ success, message }` names the attempt count and the last error; a success after retries reports how many attempts were needed, and the post-release timing/summary output surfaces it.
- The sibling retry test item's `todo` markers are removed and its tests pass, and `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` stays green.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments in `run-release.js` and the `skill/ship/SKILL.md` dev-sync description (retry policy and its scope).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `TRANSPORT_ERROR_PATTERNS` (case-insensitive regex list) and `isTransportError(err)` next to `syncDevWithMain()`.
- Extract the 4-command sequence into an inner `attemptSync()`; loop `for (attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1)` rethrowing non-transport errors immediately and sleeping `backoffMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)` between transport failures.
- Default `sleep` uses `Atomics.wait` on a `SharedArrayBuffer` (no dependency, no busy loop) and is injectable; validate `attempts >= 1`.
- Return `{ success, message, attempts }`; document the allowlist in a JSDoc block citing SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `syncDevWithMain()` (~1477-1530) plus the classifier helpers
- `tests/unit/test-post-release-dev-sync.mjs` — remove `todo` markers
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — dev-sync step description mentions the retry policy

## Impact

A transient git transport error on the post-release sync is absorbed automatically instead of needing manual recovery.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the retry test item, and serialised after the tail reorder (both edit `run-release.js`).

# Add --finish-release recovery command

Child of SA-0MWXIY8D2001DGZ0 (parent AC4, AC5, AC7, AC8). Adds the supported
`--finish-release <version>` entry point that completes a partially-applied
release tail without a new merge, PR, tag, version bump or Code Freeze marker.

## Context

A release that landed but whose tail never ran (the 2026-11-26 `v0.2.0` case)
cannot legally be finished today: re-running `run-release.js` trips the
newly-created-tag gate (exit 14, SA-0MV13B5WO008CYXA). Provenance for the
recovery path comes from `verifyReleaseMerge()` (origin tag + ancestor of
`origin/main`) instead of the pre-run tag snapshot. `sendReleaseNotification`
already accepts an explicit `{ tagCreatedByThisRun }` provenance flag and must
keep failing closed by default (SA-0MV0QEI3Q0063KH3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `--finish-release <version>` is added to `VALUE_FLAGS`, `parseReleaseArgs()` and `WRAPPER_USAGE`, and routes to a new `runFinishReleaseAction(flags)` **before** `setCodeFreezeMarker`/`runReleaseImpl`, mirroring the `--refresh-audits` pre-flight early exit.
- The action runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync — through the shared `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` helper, with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump and no Code Freeze marker.
- The newly-created-tag gate is bypassed on this path only, because the action proves the release by origin-tag + ancestor-of-`origin/main` verification instead; a normal release's exit-14 and exit-11 gates are untouched and still fire.
- `--finish-release <version>` completes a partially-applied tail idempotently: the new entry point runs only the tail — verify merge, notify, close items, cleanup, dev sync — with no merge, no PR, no tag creation, no version bump, no Code Freeze marker, and without tripping the newly-created-tag gate (provenance comes from `verifyReleaseMerge` instead). It exits 0 on success, 11 when merge verification fails, 13 on an invalid/unknown argument, and nothing is executed on argument error.
- Notification provenance is explicit on the recovery path: `sendReleaseNotification` keeps failing closed by default (a pre-existing tag is never announced); the `--finish-release` path supplies the verified-release provenance explicitly (`{ tagCreatedByThisRun: true }` once `verifyReleaseMerge` succeeds) so a confirmed release is announced exactly once, and re-running it does not double-notify (the duplicate is documented and accepted — at-most-once, no dedupe store).
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` gains the exit-code table entries (5 reserved, `--finish-release`, 11, 13) plus a partial-release recovery section, and `docs/dev/release-process.md` gains the recovery runbook for `node $(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js --finish-release <version>`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `README.md` and any relevant docs-site or wiki entries.
- The sibling `--finish-release` test item's `todo` markers are removed and its tests pass; existing `tests/unit/test-run-release-*.mjs` stay green.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Minimal Implementation

- Parse the flag into `flags.finishRelease`, validate it is a non-empty semver-ish string (else exit 13 before any side effect).
- Add `export async function runFinishReleaseAction(flags, projectRoot)` in the pre-flight area next to `runRefreshAuditsAction`'s call site (~1743): resolve root read-only, call `verifyReleaseMerge(version)` (exit 11 on failure), then `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail({ version, prUrl: null, projectRoot, dryRun, provenance: { tagCreatedByThisRun: true } })`.
- Thread a `provenance` argument through `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()` into `sendReleaseNotification` so the normal path still passes `{ preRunTags }` while the recovery path passes `{ tagCreatedByThisRun: true }`.
- Document the command, its exit codes, the at-most-once notification caveat and the recovery runbook in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/release-process.md`.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `VALUE_FLAGS` / `parseReleaseArgs()` / `WRAPPER_USAGE` (~145-250), `runFinishReleaseAction()` next to the `--refresh-audits` pre-flight (~1743)
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — confirm `{ tagCreatedByThisRun }` is sufficient; no dedupe store added (explicitly out of scope)
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — exit-code table, post-release step order, partial-release recovery section
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — recovery runbook
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-finish-release.mjs` — remove `todo` markers

## Impact

A release that already landed can be finished with one documented command instead of a hand-rolled `node -e` script, so shipped items reach `completed/done` and the announcement goes out.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the `--finish-release` test item and the tail reorder (reuses `runVerifiedPostReleaseTail()`).

# Test: large-parent Phase 2 prompt-size capture contract

## Goal

Pin the prompt-size measurement contract with a deterministic, offline fixture
that reproduces the 2026-11-24 large-parent Phase 2 shape — **before** any
production change lands (TDD).

**User story:** As the release producer, I want a large-parent Phase 2 audit to
report the size of the exact prompt it sent, so a provider error on that shape
can be diagnosed without guessing or a live provider.

## Context / evidence

Parent item `SA-0MWV3N94G007H6A9`. The failing Phase 2 call was on
`RISE-0MW7V58ZP0058NMI`: a parent with 14 children (all `completed`/`done`),
a ~18 KB description and 9 acceptance criteria. The failing runs persisted
`calls=2 parse_ok=1 provider_errors=1` with no prompt size recorded because
`_call_pi` reads `input_tokens` from the `agent_end` usage block, which a
`finish_reason: error` call may not emit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — A deterministic offline fixture represents the failing shape: a parent
  with 14+ children carrying persisted audits, a ~18 KB description and 9+
  acceptance criteria. The fixture drives the **production**
  `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` prompt-construction path (the test must not
  re-implement prompt assembly).
- AC2 — A test asserts the measured Phase 2 parent prompt size (bytes and
  estimated tokens) is captured by production code and retrievable from the
  call result / per-call timing line / debug-log entry.
- AC3 — A test asserts the prompt size is still captured on a provider-error
  (`finish_reason: error`) path where the stream carries no `agent_end` usage
  block, so the failing prompt size is never lost.
- AC4 — The tests fail against the current implementation and pass once the
  measurement change (C3) lands, and they run in the audit test suite.
- AC5 — Capture the failure with measured size: the failing Phase 2 prompt shape
  is reproduced deterministically by a fixture (large parent: 14+ children with
  persisted audits, ~18 KB description, 9+ acceptance criteria) with the failing
  prompt's measured size recorded (bytes and estimated tokens), so the size
  hypothesis can be evaluated without a live provider.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/large_parent_phase2.py` building the parent
  dict + 14 child dicts with `ac_results` and persisted-audit markers.
- Add `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2_prompt_size.py` with tests
  that mock `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (capturing the real prompt) and assert the
  measured size fields; include the provider-error variant.
- Use the production `_run_phase2_deep_analysis` entrypoint only — no copied
  prompt strings in the test.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/large_parent_phase2.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_phase2_prompt_size.py` (new)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the first, test-first slice.

## Deliverables

- Deterministic large-parent fixture.
- Failing-then-passing prompt-size capture tests.

## Impact

A large-parent Phase 2 audit will report the exact measured prompt size, so a
provider error can be diagnosed from the log alone instead of guessing.

## Summary

Add a regression test that proves **report isolation**: a run started for a SorraAgents item that observes a foreign queued entry produces no persisted audit and no `wl` write for the foreign entry, and the persisted report's acceptance-criteria and variance rows derive only from the audited item's (and its children's) own worklog data. Record the contamination mechanism this change removes, or the residual risk if it cannot be reproduced.

This covers parent `SA-0MWWE4OI1006OC42` AC5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A regression test starts an `issue` run for a SorraAgents item while the `audit-batch` queue holds at least one entry stamped with a foreign project root (and optionally a rootless legacy entry) and asserts: no `cmd_issue` call for the foreign id, no `wl update`/`wl comment` invocation naming the foreign id, and no persisted audit (`auditResult`/`audit-show`) for the foreign id.
- A companion assertion proves report isolation: the persisted Phase-2 report's acceptance-criteria and variance rows contain only ids/evidence from the audited item and its own children (no foreign id, AC text or variance row).
- The test also passes for an explicit `--batch-drain` run scoped to the audited item's project (the foreign entry is skipped, not audited).
- The contamination mechanism the change removes (or the residual risk if the report contamination cannot be reproduced) is stated in a comment on this item and summarised on the parent.
- New tests pass and are added to `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` (or the adjacent `cmd_issue` trigger test file).

## Minimal Implementation

- Build the test on the existing `cmd_issue` mocking harness: `_fake_context`, `_recording_audit_one`, a mocked `Runner` capturing every `wl` command, and `_enqueue_with_root`.
- Enqueue a foreign-rooted entry (e.g. root `/home/rgardler/projects/other`) plus a rootless legacy entry, run default `issue` and `issue --batch-drain`, and assert the captured `wl` writes and persisted report text.
- If the test reveals a second contamination vector beyond the drain, record it as a new blocking work item rather than expanding this item's scope.
- Comment the proved mechanism / residual risk on this item and the parent.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` — existing helpers and the batch-drain suite.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue` persist path and `_maybe_run_batch_drain` are the behaviour under test (no production change expected here).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` / `test_audit_runner_trigger`-style harness — reuse the established `cmd_issue` mocking patterns.

## Deliverables

- Report-isolation regression test(s).
- Documented proved mechanism or residual-risk statement on this item and the parent.

## Summary

Make `audit_runner.py issue <id>` strictly single-item by default: the post-audit batch drain runs **only** when the operator passes `--batch-drain`. `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` no longer switches the drain on (it loses its "auto-on" meaning) and `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` remains a hard disable of an explicitly requested drain. The audited item's own children keep their current in-scope behaviour.

This is the primary behaviour fix for parent `SA-0MWWE4OI1006OC42` (desired change 1).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `audit_runner.py issue <id>` audits **only** `<id>` (and, unchanged, its children): with two or more foreign entries queued in the `audit-batch` queue, a default `cmd_issue` invocation calls neither `_maybe_run_batch_drain` nor `_batch_drain_cycle`, audits none of them, leaves every entry queued, and its exit code and persisted verdict are identical to a run against an empty queue.
- The post-audit drain is **explicit** for `issue`: it runs only when the operator passes `--batch-drain`; neither the default invocation (`batch_drain=None`) nor `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` set to any value other than `0` can trigger it.
- `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=0` still disables an explicitly requested `--batch-drain` run (hard disable preserved), and `--no-batch-drain` keeps the drain off.
- `_batch_audit_one` continues to pass `batch_drain=False` so a drain can never recurse.
- Regression tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` cover default-off, the `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN` semantics matrix, and exit-code/verdict invariance, and pass together with the existing batch-drain suite.

## Minimal Implementation

- Change the `cmd_issue` tail trigger (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ~18681) from `batch_drain is not False` to `batch_drain is True`, still gated on `_batch_drain_enabled()`.
- Redefine `_batch_drain_enabled()` (~5722) as a pure hard-disable check: `os.environ.get(AUDIT_BATCH_DISABLE_ENV, "1") != "0"` stays, but its docstring and the surrounding constants must state it is only an opt-out for an explicit request, never a trigger.
- Update the `cmd_issue` docstring (`*batch_drain*` paragraph, ~18321), the `--batch-drain` help text (~19288) and the `--no-batch-drain` help text to describe the new default.
- Tests: default invocation does not call `_maybe_run_batch_drain`; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=1`/unset does not enable it; `=0` blocks an explicit request; two foreign queued entries leave `queue_remaining` unchanged and the primary verdict/exit code identical.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `cmd_issue` tail trigger (~18681), `_maybe_run_batch_drain` (~18690), `_batch_drain_enabled` (~5722), CLI flags (~19288), `cmd_issue` docstring (~18321).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_batch_drain.py` — existing `_fake_context`, `_enqueue_with_root`, `_recording_audit_one` helpers; extend for default-off and env-matrix coverage.

## Deliverables

- Code change making the `issue` drain explicit opt-in.
- Updated docstrings and CLI help text.
- Unit/regression tests proving default-off and env semantics.

## Constraints

- Do not touch `cmd_batch` (child `SA-…` project-scoped drain item owns scoping; the `batch` subcommand stays the cross-project entry point).

## TDD

Write the failing test(s) first (default invocation must not drain; `AUDIT_BATCH_DRAIN=1` must not enable), then make them pass.

A release-gate or agent audit of one item finishes auditing that item and stops, so its duration and verdict no longer depend on other projects' queued work.
